_about: The Instituta Cnuti in the translator’s order, assembled by tools/incn/reading.py from the clause files (“beside”: printed by Liebermann beside the law it translates; “list”: printed in his list, Gesetze I pp. 612–615).

passages.text: <seg type="parallel"><label>H Di</label>Incipiunt <hi rend="spaced">quędam</hi> instituta de legibus regum Anglorum (<hi rend="italic">H</hi>; <hi rend="spaced">instituta secundum Cnud regem</hi> Anglorum <hi rend="italic">Di</hi>).</seg><seg type="parallel"><label>Ip Hunt (Interpolator of Henry of Huntingdon)</label>Incipit <hi rend="spaced">lex que Anglice Danelage</hi><hi rend="spaced"> est uocata, Latine uero lex Dacorum est interpretata, ab inuictissimo et glorioso</hi> <hi rend="small">rege Anglorum, Dacorum, Norwagenorum, Sueuorum</hi> Cnuto instituta et diligenter custodita.</seg>
passages.en: <seg type="parallel"><label>H Di</label>Here begin <hi rend="spaced">certain</hi> institutes concerning the laws of the kings of the English (<hi rend="italic">H</hi>; <hi rend="spaced">institutes according to King Cnut</hi> of the English <hi rend="italic">Di</hi>).</seg><seg type="parallel"><label>Ip Hunt (Interpolator of Henry of Huntingdon)</label>Here begins <hi rend="spaced">the law which in English is called <hi rend="italic">Danelage</hi>, but in Latin is rendered as the law of the Danes,</hi> instituted and diligently kept <hi rend="spaced">by the most invincible and glorious</hi> <hi rend="small">king of the English, Danes, Norwegians, Swedes</hi>, Cnut.</seg>

passages.text: Hęc est institutio, quam Cnud rex cum <hi rend="spaced">consilio</hi><hi rend="spaced"> principum</hi> suorum sapientium ad laudem Dei et honorem sui ipsius et profectum <hi rend="bold">totius regni</hi><hi rend="bold"> cui preerat</hi> instituit.
passages.en: This is the institution which King Cnut, with the <hi rend="spaced">counsel of the chief men</hi>, his wise men, instituted to the praise of God and the honour of himself and the benefit <hi rend="bold">of the whole kingdom over which he ruled</hi>.

passages.text: Inprimis, quod super omnia uellet semper unum Deum colere, amare, honorare, unam fidem Christi unanimiter seruare, ęcclesias Dei in pace et securitate custodire <hi rend="spaced">easdemque</hi> sepius frequentare <hi rend="bold">pro quiete et stabilitate regni sui pro-</hi>
passages.en: First, that above all things he would always worship one God, love, honour [him], keep with one mind the one faith of Christ, guard the churches of God in peace and security, <hi rend="spaced">and the same</hi> frequent more often, <hi rend="bold">for the quiet and stability of his kingdom and for …</hi>

passages.text: que <hi rend="spaced">salute corporis et animę suę</hi>.
passages.en: … <hi rend="spaced">the salvation of his body and soul</hi>.

passages.text: Omnis <hi rend="spaced">itaque</hi> ęcclesia secundum normam iusticię <hi rend="spaced">debet</hi> esse in propria pace et securitate Dei; et omni Christiano conuenit maximam reuerentiam <hi rend="spaced">exhibere ęcclesiis Dei</hi>; pax enim et securitas Dei summa diligentia promerenda et tenenda est, deinde pax et securitas regis.
passages.en: Every church <hi rend="spaced">therefore</hi> according to the rule of justice <hi rend="spaced">ought</hi> to be in God's own peace and security; and it befits every Christian <hi rend="spaced">to show the churches of God</hi> the greatest reverence; for the peace and security of God is to be earned and held with the utmost diligence, and next the peace and security of the king.

passages.text: Quare ęquissimum est, ut pax ęcclesiarum Dei infra parietes et pax <hi rend="spaced">data manu</hi> Christiani regis semper stet inuiolata; et qui aliquam, ęcclesię <hi rend="spaced">scilicet aut regis pacem</hi>, fregerit, careat <hi rend="spaced">omnibus bonis suis</hi> et uita, nisi rex illi parcere uoluerit.
passages.en: Wherefore it is most just that the peace of the churches of God within the walls and the peace <hi rend="spaced">given by the hand</hi> of a Christian king always stand inviolate; and whoever breaks either, <hi rend="spaced">namely the peace of the church or of the king</hi>, let him lose <hi rend="spaced">all his goods</hi> and life, unless the king will spare him.

passages.text: Quodsi dehinc aliquis pacem ęcclesiarum Dei ita uiolauerit, ut infra parietes <hi rend="spaced">homicidium faciat</hi>, hoc sit inemendabile, persequaturque talem omnis qui <hi rend="spaced">uoluerit</hi> Dei esse amicus, nisi hoc fiat, ut effugiat et talem locum <hi rend="bold">aut hominem</hi> requirat, pro qua <hi rend="spaced">requisitione</hi> ei rex uitam condonet, <hi rend="spaced">attamen</hi> ad plenam emendationem.
passages.en: But if henceforth anyone so violates the peace of the churches of God that he <hi rend="spaced">commits homicide</hi> within the walls, this shall be unatonable, and let everyone who <hi rend="spaced">wishes</hi> to be a friend of God pursue such a man, unless it happens that he escapes and seeks such a place <hi rend="bold">or man</hi> that for this <hi rend="spaced">seeking</hi> the king grants him his life, <hi rend="spaced">yet</hi> on condition of full amends.

passages.text: Si autem ad emendationem peruenerit, et rex hoc permiserit, ante omnia ęcclesię pacem fractam pleniter emendet secundum plenam forisfacturam, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli nominant</hi> múndbrece, <seg type="recension">(et)</seg> ęcclesię reconciliationem adquirat, <seg type="recension">(et)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">plenam emendationem</hi> parentibus et domino occisi persoluat, quam Angli mæibote et manbote <hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>, et super omnia Deo satisfaciat <hi rend="bold">secundum decretum episcopi</hi>.
passages.en: But if he comes to amends, and the king permits it, before all things let him fully make amends for the broken peace of the church according to the full forfeiture, <hi rend="spaced">which the English name</hi> <hi rend="italic">múndbrece</hi> [breach of protection], <seg type="recension">(and)</seg> obtain reconciliation for the church, <seg type="recension">(and)</seg> pay <hi rend="spaced">full amends</hi> to the kinsmen and the lord of the slain man, which the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">mæibote</hi> and <hi rend="italic">manbote</hi> [compensation to kin and to lord], and above all make satisfaction to God <hi rend="bold">according to the bishop's decree</hi>.

passages.text: Sin <hi rend="spaced">autem</hi> aliter de uiuis pax ęcclesię uiolata fuerit uel pugnando uel <hi rend="spaced">rapiendo</hi> uel per quicquid sit,
passages.en: If <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> the peace of the church is otherwise violated by the living, either by fighting or by <hi rend="spaced">robbing</hi> or by whatever it may be,

passages.text: imprimis semper fiat emendatio ęcclesię secundum qualitatem <seg type="recension">(et dignitatem)</seg> eius.
passages.en: first of all let amends always be made to the church according to its quality <seg type="recension">(and dignity)</seg>.

passages.text: Non <hi rend="spaced">enim</hi> sunt omnes ęcclesię <hi rend="spaced">unius eiusdemque</hi> honoris, quamuis habeant <hi rend="spaced">unam eandemque</hi> consecrationem.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">For</hi> not all churches are of <hi rend="spaced">one and the same</hi> honour, although they have <hi rend="spaced">one and the same</hi> consecration.

passages.text: Principales <hi rend="spaced">autem</hi> ęcclesię, <hi rend="bold">sicut</hi><hi rend="bold"> episcopatus </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(et</hi><hi rend="bold"> abbatię)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">,</hi> talem <hi rend="spaced">emendationem</hi> uiolatę pacis secundum legem Anglorum <hi rend="spaced">habere</hi><hi rend="spaced"> debent</hi>: mundam regis, hoc est quinque libras; <hi rend="bold">secundum</hi><hi rend="bold"> certe</hi><hi rend="bold"> legem Danorum octo</hi><hi rend="bold"> libras.</hi><seg type="parallel"><label>Cb</label>Mediocres autem ecclesie, <hi rend="bold">ut abatie et canonicatus,</hi> iuxta forisfacturam regis, uidelicet <hi rend="bold">XXC</hi> solidos, <hi rend="bold">hoc est qaatuor libras.</hi> Minores quidem ecclesie, hoc est ubi seruitium fit, et tamen cimiterium habent, LX solidos <hi rend="bold">hoc est tres libras.</hi> <hi rend="spaced">Minime uero ecclesie</hi>, quam <hi rend="spaced">Angli</hi> feldcherche dicunt, id est carentes cimiterio, XXX sol.</seg><seg type="parallel"><label>H Di Lb S Ct Jo</label>Mediocris autem ęcclesię <hi rend="bold">duas libras,</hi> hoc est secundum forisfacturam regis, et adhuc minoris ęcclesię, hoc est ubi parum seruitii fit, et tamen cimiterium habet, forisfactura est <hi rend="bold">unius</hi><hi rend="bold"> libre;</hi> minimę uero ęcclesię, quam Angli feldcirice uocant, <hi rend="bold">octoginta denariorum.</hi></seg>
passages.en: The chief churches <hi rend="spaced">however</hi>, <hi rend="bold">such as bishoprics </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(and abbeys)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">ought to have</hi> such <hi rend="spaced">amends</hi> for violated peace according to the law of the English: the king's <hi rend="italic">mund</hi> [protection], that is five pounds; <hi rend="bold">but according to the law of the Danes, certainly, eight pounds.</hi><seg type="parallel"><label>Cb</label>But middling churches, <hi rend="bold">such as abbeys and houses of canons,</hi> according to the king's forfeiture, namely <hi rend="bold">XXC</hi> shillings, <hi rend="bold">that is four pounds.</hi> The lesser churches, that is where service is held and yet they have a cemetery, 60 shillings, <hi rend="bold">that is three pounds.</hi> <hi rend="spaced">But the least churches</hi>, which <hi rend="spaced">the English</hi> call <hi rend="italic">feldcherche</hi> [field-church], that is those lacking a cemetery, 30 shillings.</seg><seg type="parallel"><label>H Di Lb S Ct Jo</label>But for a middling church <hi rend="bold">two pounds,</hi> that is according to the king's forfeiture, and further for a lesser church, that is where little service is held and yet it has a cemetery, the forfeiture is <hi rend="bold">one pound;</hi> but for the least church, which the English call <hi rend="italic">feldcirice</hi> [field-church], <hi rend="bold">eighty pence.</hi></seg>

passages.text: Omnibus <hi rend="spaced">igitur</hi> Christianis iustissime decet <seg type="recension">(cum)</seg> summa diligentia semper uenerari <hi rend="spaced">reliquias sanctorum</hi>, ordinatos et domos sanctificatas et unumquemque ordinem secundum mensuram <hi rend="bold">et uitam suam</hi> honorare.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Therefore</hi> it most justly befits all Christians always to venerate <seg type="recension">(with)</seg> the utmost diligence <hi rend="spaced">the relics of the saints</hi>, and to honour the ordained and hallowed houses and each order according to its measure <hi rend="bold">and its life</hi>.

passages.text: Propterea qui <hi rend="bold">uult</hi> cognoscat, multum est et magnum quod sacerdos habet ad faciendum populo ad necessitatem <seg type="recension">(profectum)</seg>, si ipse Domino recte placuerit <seg type="recension">(qui Domino <hi rend="spaced">suo desiderat et studet</hi> iuste placere)</seg>.
passages.en: Therefore let him who <hi rend="bold">wishes</hi> know that much and great is what the priest has to do for the people for their need <seg type="recension">(benefit)</seg>, if he himself rightly pleases the Lord <seg type="recension">(who <hi rend="spaced">desires and strives</hi> to please <hi rend="spaced">his</hi> Lord justly)</seg>.

passages.text: Magna enim est adiuratio et maior consecratio, quę demonia eiciunt et in fugam uertunt, quotiens <hi rend="spaced">infans baptizatur</hi> aut corpus Domini consecratur; <hi rend="spaced">certe</hi> angeli circumuolant et per Dei uirtutem sacerdoti auxilium prębent, facta muniunt, quotiens Christo digne seruiunt.
passages.en: For great is the adjuration and greater the consecration, which cast out demons and put them to flight, whenever <hi rend="spaced">an infant is baptized</hi> or the Lord's body is consecrated; <hi rend="spaced">certainly</hi> angels fly around and by God's power give help to the priest and protect his deeds, whenever they serve Christ worthily.

passages.text: Sic etiam semper faciunt, cum deuote Christum inuocant pro populi necessitate et <hi rend="spaced">Deo</hi> preces fundunt; et ideo in tali ordine <seg type="recension">(ut <hi rend="spaced">diximus</hi>)</seg> magna debet esse discretio et <hi rend="spaced">consideratio</hi>.
passages.en: So too they always do, when they devoutly invoke Christ for the people's need and pour out prayers to <hi rend="spaced">God</hi>; and therefore in such an order <seg type="recension">(as <hi rend="spaced">we have said</hi>)</seg> there ought to be great discretion and <hi rend="spaced">consideration</hi>.

passages.text: Si contigerit presbyterum regulariter et <hi rend="spaced">caste</hi> uiuentem calumniari de latrocinio aut de incantatione uel de aliqua huiusmodi <seg type="recension">(simili)</seg> re, et negauerit, ita se purgabit, si audet: missam celebret et per corpus Domini solus de una appellatione, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> anfealde spæce, se purget.
passages.en: If it happens that a priest living by rule and <hi rend="spaced">chastely</hi> is accused of theft or of sorcery or of any such <seg type="recension">(similar)</seg> matter, and he denies it, he shall clear himself thus, if he dares: let him celebrate mass and clear himself alone by the body of the Lord of a single accusation, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">anfealde spæce</hi> [single charge].

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">autem</hi> diaconus qui regulariter uiuit calumniatur simpla appellatione, acceptis duobus diaconibus secum, purget se.
passages.en: If <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> a deacon who lives by rule is accused by a single accusation, let him clear himself, taking two deacons with him.

passages.text: Et si tres calumnię fuerint, assumat VI <hi rend="spaced">secum</hi> et ipse sit septimus <seg type="recension">(sex secum <hi rend="spaced">diaconibus</hi> acceptis, ita se purget)</seg>.
passages.en: And if there are three accusations, let him take six <hi rend="spaced">with him</hi> and himself be the seventh <seg type="recension">(having taken six <hi rend="spaced">deacons</hi> with him, let him so clear himself)</seg>.

passages.text: Si uulgaris <seg type="recension">(popularis)</seg> presbyter calumniatur, qui non regulariter uiuit, <hi rend="spaced">simpla</hi> appellatione <seg type="recension">(de supradictis)</seg>, purget se sicut diaconus qui regulariter uiuit.
passages.en: If a common <seg type="recension">(popular)</seg> priest, who does not live by rule, is accused by a <hi rend="spaced">single</hi> accusation <seg type="recension">(of the above-said)</seg>, let him clear himself like a deacon who lives by rule.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="bold">aduena aut</hi> <hi rend="bold">peregrinus</hi> ordinatus calumniatur de <hi rend="spaced">iam nominatis</hi> criminibus, qui adiutorium <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">aliud auxilium</hi>)</seg> non habet, eat ad panem benedictum, quem <hi rend="spaced">Angli</hi> corsnade <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi>, et ibi inueniet quod Deo placuerit.
passages.en: If an ordained <hi rend="bold">stranger or</hi> <hi rend="bold">foreigner</hi> is accused of the <hi rend="spaced">already named</hi> crimes, who has no helper <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">other aid</hi>)</seg>, let him go to the blessed bread, which <hi rend="spaced">the English</hi> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">corsnade</hi> [<hi rend="italic">corsnæd</hi>, ordeal morsel], and there he will find what pleases God.

passages.text: Si quis ordinatus calumniatur de homicidio, quod fuisset in facto aut in consilio, purget se cum parentibus suis, qui possunt emendare aut deportare.
passages.en: If any ordained man is accused of homicide, that he had been in it by deed or by counsel, let him clear himself with his kinsmen, who can pay the amends or bear [the feud].

passages.text: Si non habet parentes, purget se cum sociis uel incipiat ieiunare et sic eat ad panem benedictum, <hi rend="spaced">de quo supra diximus</hi>, et ibi inueniet quod Deo placitum fuerit <seg type="recension">(inueniat Deo placita)</seg>.
passages.en: If he has no kinsmen, let him clear himself with companions or begin to fast and so go to the blessed bread, <hi rend="spaced">of which we spoke above</hi>, and there he will find what has pleased God <seg type="recension">(let him find what pleases God)</seg>.

passages.text: Nullus monachus monasterialis debet emendare homicidium nec petere emendationem homicidii, <hi rend="bold">licet sit parens occisoris</hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(occidentium)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold"> uel occisi</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">quia</hi> ubi intrat <hi rend="spaced">monasterium</hi> pro tenenda regula, relinquit <hi rend="spaced">ea quę sunt secularia</hi> . . . .
passages.en: No monk of a monastery ought to pay amends for homicide nor seek amends for homicide, <hi rend="bold">though he be a kinsman of the slayer</hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(of the slayers)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold"> or of the slain</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">because</hi> when he enters the <hi rend="spaced">monastery</hi> to keep the rule, he leaves behind <hi rend="spaced">the things that are secular</hi> . . . .

passages.text: Si quis commendauerit alterius monacho pecuniam <hi rend="bold">aut aliquid tale</hi> <hi rend="spaced">ad custodiendum</hi> sine licentia <hi rend="bold">prelati</hi> sui, et <hi rend="spaced">monachus illud perdiderit, sit illi perditum qui</hi> sine licentia <hi rend="bold">prelati</hi> <hi rend="spaced">eius</hi> <hi rend="spaced">monacho commendauit</hi> . . . .
passages.en: If anyone commends money <hi rend="bold">or any such thing</hi> to another man's monk <hi rend="spaced">for safekeeping</hi> without the leave of his <hi rend="bold">prelate</hi>, and <hi rend="spaced">the monk loses it, let it be lost to him who</hi> without the leave of <hi rend="spaced">his</hi> <hi rend="bold">prelate</hi> <hi rend="spaced">commended it to the monk</hi> . . . .

passages.text: Et si tres <hi rend="spaced">appellationes</hi> fuerint, secum acceptis duobus presbyteris, purget se, <hi rend="spaced">sicut</hi> prędiximus, si audet . . . .
passages.en: And if there are three <hi rend="spaced">accusations</hi>, let him clear himself, taking two priests with him, <hi rend="spaced">as</hi> we said before, if he dares . . . .

passages.text: Presbyter si <hi rend="bold">calumniatus et conuictus fuerit,</hi> quod stetisset in falso testimonio aut iurasset cum periuris aut fuisset socius aut conscius latrocinii, deponatur á communione et á societate ordinatorum et careat liberalitate eorum, <hi rend="bold">quod</hi><hi rend="bold"> Angli uocant þegenscipe</hi>, nisi profundius satisfaciat Deo et hominibus secundum pręceptum episcopi sui, et fideiussores inueniat, quod ab eo tempore amplius cessabit ab eiusmodi <hi rend="spaced">operibus</hi>.
passages.en: A priest, if he <hi rend="bold">has been accused and convicted</hi> that he stood in false witness or swore with perjurers or was an accomplice or privy to theft, let him be put out of the communion and fellowship of the ordained and lose their noble rank, <hi rend="bold">which the English call <hi rend="italic">þegenscipe</hi></hi> [thegnship], unless he makes deeper satisfaction to God and men according to his bishop's command, and finds sureties that from that time on he will cease from such <hi rend="spaced">works</hi>.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">negauerit</hi> et purgare sé uoluerit, secundum culpę modum et quantitatem sé purget.
passages.en: But if he <hi rend="spaced">denies</hi> it and wishes to clear himself, let him clear himself according to the manner and quantity of the guilt.

passages.text: Hoc etiam statuimus, ut <hi rend="spaced">unusquisque</hi>, cuiuscumque ordinis <hi rend="spaced">aut</hi><hi rend="spaced"> sexus sit</hi>, seruet ordinem suum.
passages.en: This also we decree, that <hi rend="spaced">everyone</hi>, of whatever order <hi rend="spaced">or sex he be</hi>, keep his order.

passages.text: Et pręcipue hoc pręcipimus seruis et ancillis Dei, uidelicet episcopis, abbatibus, <hi rend="spaced">abbatissis</hi>, monachis, sanctimonialibus, canonicis, <hi rend="spaced">presbyteris</hi>, nonnis, ut regulariter uiuant <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">sicut</hi><hi rend="spaced"> diximus</hi>)</seg> secundum ordinem uniuscuiusque,
passages.en: And especially we command this to the servants and handmaids of God, namely bishops, abbots, <hi rend="spaced">abbesses</hi>, monks, holy women, canons, <hi rend="spaced">priests</hi>, nuns, that they live by rule <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">as we have said</hi>)</seg> according to the order of each,

passages.text: castitatem seruent, ab ira Dei sibi caueant <hi rend="bold">et alios uiuendo et monendo castigent,</hi> ut se ab infernali incendio custodiant.
passages.en: keep chastity, beware of the wrath of God <hi rend="bold">and chasten others by living and admonishing,</hi> so that they guard themselves from the fire of hell.

passages.text: Optime enim norunt <hi rend="spaced">episcopi</hi> et cęteri ordines, quos <hi rend="spaced">supra memoraui</hi> <seg type="recension">(nominaui)</seg>, quod illis nullo modo licet communionem mulierum habere nec cum illis coire.
passages.en: For the <hi rend="spaced">bishops</hi> and the other orders whom I <hi rend="spaced">have mentioned above</hi> <seg type="recension">(named)</seg> know very well that it is in no way lawful for them to have intercourse with women nor to lie with them.

passages.text: Qui autem abhinc a tali <hi rend="spaced">opere</hi> cessare et castitatem custodire uoluerit <seg type="recension">(studuerit)</seg>, misericordiam Dei habeat et secundum dignitatem seculi liberalitatem, <hi rend="spaced">quam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi> þegenscipe.
passages.en: But he who henceforth wishes <seg type="recension">(strives)</seg> to cease from such <hi rend="spaced">work</hi> and to keep chastity, let him have the mercy of God and, according to worldly dignity, the noble rank <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þegenscipe</hi> [thegnship].

passages.text: Omnem etiam Christianum obnixe <hi rend="spaced">precamur</hi>, fornicationem deuitare, leges et <hi rend="spaced">praecepta</hi> Dei diligenter custodire.
passages.en: We also earnestly <hi rend="spaced">pray</hi> every Christian to avoid fornication and to keep diligently the laws and <hi rend="spaced">precepts</hi> of God.

passages.text: Hoc quoque rogamus et in nomine <hi rend="spaced">Domini</hi> pręcipimus, ut nullus Christianus accipiat sibi uxorem infra sextum <hi rend="bold">genu</hi>, nec in relicta uxore, quę ita <hi rend="spaced">fuit</hi> propinquo parenti <hi rend="spaced">coniuncta</hi>, nec in parente uxoris suę, quam ante habuit;
passages.en: This also we ask and command in the name of the <hi rend="spaced">Lord</hi>, that no Christian take to himself a wife within the sixth <hi rend="bold">knee</hi> [degree], nor the widow who <hi rend="spaced">was</hi> thus <hi rend="spaced">joined</hi> to a near kinsman, nor a kinswoman of the wife whom he had before;

passages.text: nec in compatra sua nec in consecrata <hi rend="bold">sanctimoniali</hi> aut nonna nec in alterius relicta, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> oþres <hi rend="bold">mannes</hi> ælǽte: talibus, <hi rend="spaced">ut diximus</hi>, nemo Christianus se iungat;
passages.en: nor his fellow godparent, nor a consecrated <hi rend="bold">holy woman</hi> or nun, nor another man's widow, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">oþres <hi rend="bold">mannes</hi> ælǽte</hi> [another man's relict]: to such, <hi rend="spaced">as we said</hi>, let no Christian join himself;

passages.text: nec habeat nisi unam uxorem, quę sit ei legitime desponsata, eaque sola, dum uiuit, <hi rend="bold">sana et infirma,</hi> sit contentus.
passages.en: nor let him have more than one wife, who is lawfully betrothed to him, and with her alone, while she lives, <hi rend="bold">healthy and sick,</hi> let him be content.

passages.text: Sollicite <hi rend="spaced">quoque</hi> studeamus rectitudines Dei persoluere:
passages.en: Let us <hi rend="spaced">also</hi> carefully strive to pay God's dues:

passages.text: scilicet elemosinas carrucarum, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> súlhælmesse, quindecim dies post Pascha et <hi rend="spaced">decimas pecorum et pecudum</hi> in Pentecosten, frugum <seg type="recension">(et fructuum)</seg> terrę in festiuitate Omnium sanctorum.
passages.en: namely the plough-alms, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">súlhælmesse</hi> [plough-alms], fifteen days after Easter, and <hi rend="spaced">the tithes of cattle and small beasts</hi> at Pentecost, [and] of the crops <seg type="recension">(and fruits)</seg> of the earth at the feast of All Saints.

passages.text: Si quis decimam, sicut carruca <hi rend="spaced">perarat</hi>, dare noluerit, <hi rend="spaced">adeant</hi> eum prępositus regis et prępositus episcopi, prępositus etiam domini, cuius <hi rend="bold">in capite</hi> terra est, et presbyter ęcclesię, ad <hi rend="spaced">quam</hi> decima illa pertinet <seg type="recension">(eant)</seg>, et, <hi rend="bold">si aliter non possunt,</hi> ui aufe<hi rend="spaced">rant decimam et dent</hi> ęcclesię, ad quam <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi>)</seg> pertinet; nonam autem partem dimittant illi <seg type="recension">(dent ei)</seg>, <hi rend="spaced">qui iniuste decimam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">retinuit</hi>; octo uero partes diuidantur inter dominum terrę et episcopum, cuiuscunque homo sit, regis, <hi rend="bold">comitis</hi> aut liberalis hominis, quem Angli þegen uocant.
passages.en: If anyone will not give the tithe, as the plough <hi rend="spaced">ploughs it</hi>, let the king's reeve and the bishop's reeve, and also the reeve of the lord whose land it is <hi rend="bold">in chief</hi>, and the priest of the church to <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> that tithe belongs <hi rend="spaced">go to</hi> him <seg type="recension">(go)</seg>, and, <hi rend="bold">if they cannot otherwise,</hi> let them by force take <hi rend="spaced">away the tithe and give it</hi> to the church to which it <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">rightfully</hi>)</seg> belongs; but let them leave the ninth part to him <seg type="recension">(give to him)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">who unjustly</hi> <hi rend="spaced">retained the tithe</hi>; and let the eight parts be divided between the lord of the land and the bishop, whosesoever man he be, the king's, an <hi rend="bold">earl's</hi> or a free man of rank's (thegn's), whom the English call <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi> [thegn].

passages.text: Pecunia <hi rend="spaced">autem</hi> <seg type="recension">(sancti)</seg> Petri, quam Angli uocant Romescot, <hi rend="spaced">sit persoluta</hi> in festo sancti Petri <hi rend="bold">in principio Augusti mensis</hi> . . .
passages.en: The money <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> of <seg type="recension">(Saint)</seg> Peter, which the English call <hi rend="italic">Romescot</hi> [Rome-scot], <hi rend="spaced">is to be paid</hi> on the feast of Saint Peter <hi rend="bold">at the beginning of the month of August</hi> . . .

passages.text: Et qui non eo die persoluerit, <hi rend="bold">etiam si est unus</hi> <hi rend="bold">denarius,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">qui dare eum debuit</hi> <hi rend="spaced">et non dedit</hi>, accipiat eundem et insuper triginta denarios et portet Romę; <hi rend="spaced">et cum redierit</hi>, tale signum secum reportet, ut certum sit, <hi rend="spaced">quod Romę fuerit</hi> <hi rend="spaced">et Beato Petro ibi triginta et unum denarium, sicut statutum est</hi>, persoluerit; cum autem reuersus fuerit domi, persoluat regi <hi rend="bold">quadraginta</hi> solidos.
passages.en: And whoever has not paid on that day, <hi rend="bold">even if it is one</hi> <hi rend="bold">penny,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">who ought to give it</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and did not give it</hi>, let him take the same and thirty pence besides and carry it to Rome; <hi rend="spaced">and when he returns</hi>, let him bring back with him such a token that it be certain <hi rend="spaced">that he was at Rome</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and to Blessed Peter there thirty-one pence, as is decreed,</hi> has paid; and when he has come back home, let him pay the king <hi rend="bold">forty</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Si uero idem homo secundo hoc retinuerit, <hi rend="spaced">similiter omnino faciat</hi>.
passages.en: But if the same man withholds it a second time, <hi rend="spaced">let him do entirely the same</hi>.

passages.text: Tertio autem si <hi rend="spaced">retinuerit, auferantur</hi> ei omnia bona sua.
passages.en: But if a third time he <hi rend="spaced">withholds it, let there be taken from</hi> him all his goods.

passages.text: . . . . <hi rend="spaced">Scotum ad luminaria,</hi> quod Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> lihtgescot, ter in anno <seg type="recension">(uno)</seg> detur de unaquaque hyda <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">id</hi><hi rend="bold"> est suling</hi>)</seg>: cera unius oboli in uigilia Paschę, in uigilia Sanctę Marię <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">in</hi><hi rend="bold"> mense Augusto</hi>)</seg>, <hi rend="spaced">in uigilia Omnium</hi> sanctorum . . . .
passages.en: . . . . <hi rend="spaced">The scot for lights,</hi> which the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">lihtgescot</hi> [light-scot], is to be given three times in the year <seg type="recension">(one)</seg> from each hide <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">that is, <hi rend="italic">suling</hi></hi>)</seg>: wax worth one halfpenny on Easter Eve, on the eve of Saint Mary <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">in the month of August</hi>)</seg>, <hi rend="spaced">on the eve of All</hi> Saints . . . .

passages.text: Si liberalis homo, quem <hi rend="spaced">Angli</hi> þegen uocant, habet in alodio <seg type="recension">(id est bocland)</seg> suo ęcclesiam, quę habeat cimiterium, tertiam partem decimę proprię <hi rend="spaced">terrę</hi> suę det illi ęcclesię.
passages.en: If a free man of rank (thegn), whom <hi rend="spaced">the English</hi> call <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi> [thegn], has on his freehold <seg type="recension">(that is <hi rend="italic">bocland</hi> [bookland])</seg> a church which has a cemetery, let him give a third part of the tithe of his own <hi rend="spaced">land</hi> to that church.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">alius</hi> habet ęcclesiam, quę cimiterium non habeat, de <hi rend="spaced">nouem partibus bonorum suorum</hi> det ęcclesię suę . . . .
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">another</hi> has a church which has no cemetery, let him give to his church out of <hi rend="spaced">the nine parts of his goods</hi> . . . .

passages.text: Omnes autem decimę reddantur <hi rend="bold">antiquis</hi> ęcclesiis, ad quas <hi rend="bold">iuste</hi> parrochiani <hi rend="spaced">pertinent</hi>, tam de dominio liberalis hominis, id est þegnes, quam de terra uillanorum, <hi rend="spaced">id est</hi> <hi rend="bold">tunmannes</hi>, sicut carruca perarat.
passages.en: But let all tithes be rendered to the <hi rend="bold">old</hi> churches to which the parishioners <hi rend="bold">rightfully</hi> <hi rend="spaced">belong</hi>, both from the demesne of a noble, that is <hi rend="italic">þegnes</hi> [a thegn's], and from the land of villeins, <hi rend="spaced">that is</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">tunmannes</hi></hi> [townsmen's], as the plough ploughs it.

passages.text: . . . . <hi rend="spaced">Omne uero</hi> ęcclesiasticum donum, quod <hi rend="spaced">Angli</hi> ciricsceat uocant, detur antiquis ęcclesiis; quod sit persolutum in festiuitate sancti Martini; si quis ultra illum diem illud retinuerit, reddat illud episcopo et undecies persoluat ei et regi <hi rend="bold">quadraginta</hi> solidos . . .
passages.en: . . . . <hi rend="spaced">But every</hi> church gift, which <hi rend="spaced">the English</hi> call <hi rend="italic">ciricsceat</hi> [church-scot], is to be given to the old churches; and let it be paid on the feast of Saint Martin; if anyone withholds it beyond that day, let him render it to the bishop and pay it elevenfold and to the king <hi rend="bold">forty</hi> shillings . . .

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">corpus</hi><hi rend="spaced"> parentis aut</hi> <hi rend="spaced">amici sui</hi> de propria parrochia <hi rend="spaced">alias portare</hi> ad sepeliendum uoluerit, faciat prius rectitudinem parrochię, ad quam pertinet, scilicet redditus, quod Angli saulescot uocant, quod recte <seg type="recension">(iuste)</seg> persolui debet ad apertum sepulchrum.
passages.en: If anyone wishes <hi rend="spaced">to carry</hi> the <hi rend="spaced">body of his kinsman or</hi> <hi rend="spaced">friend</hi> from his own parish <hi rend="spaced">elsewhere</hi> for burial, let him first do right to the parish to which he belongs, namely the due which the English call <hi rend="italic">saulescot</hi> [soul-scot], which ought rightly <seg type="recension">(justly)</seg> to be paid at the open grave.

passages.text: Solempnitates <hi rend="spaced">sanctorum</hi> diligenter <seg type="recension">(ab omnibus)</seg> celebrentur. Et Dominici dies a <hi rend="spaced">pręcedentis</hi> Sabbati hora nona usque ad lucem <hi rend="spaced">sequentis</hi> ferię secundę feriantur; alię autem festiuitates et ieiunia districte custodiantur, sicut <seg type="recension">(in <hi rend="spaced">domo</hi> <hi rend="spaced">statutum</hi> est et preceptum)</seg> praecipitur.
passages.en: Let the solemnities <hi rend="spaced">of the saints</hi> be diligently <seg type="recension">(by all)</seg> celebrated. And let Sundays be kept as holidays from the ninth hour of the <hi rend="spaced">preceding</hi> Saturday until the dawn of the <hi rend="spaced">following</hi> Monday; and let the other festivals and fasts be strictly kept, as <seg type="recension">(is <hi rend="spaced">decreed</hi> and commanded in the <hi rend="spaced">house</hi>)</seg> is commanded.

passages.text: Interdicimus <hi rend="spaced">etiam</hi> mercatum dierum Dominicorum et omnia popularia placita, nisi maxima sit necessitas.
passages.en: We <hi rend="spaced">also</hi> forbid Sunday markets and all popular courts, unless there be very great necessity.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Opera quoque</hi> uenatoria et omnia secularia negotia <hi rend="spaced">prohibemus</hi>.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Also the works</hi> of hunting and all secular business <hi rend="spaced">we prohibit</hi>.

passages.text: Legitima etiam ieiunia et <hi rend="bold">uigilię sanctorum</hi><hi rend="bold">,</hi> sanctę Marię scilicet et omnium apostolorum, excepto Philippi et Iacobi propter pascalia festa, et ieiunia omnium sextarum feriarum, nisi sit festiuitas, <hi rend="spaced">teneantur</hi>.
passages.en: Also let the lawful fasts and the <hi rend="bold">vigils of the saints,</hi> namely of Saint Mary and of all the apostles, except Philip and James because of the Easter feasts, and the fasts of all Fridays, unless it be a festival, <hi rend="spaced">be kept</hi>.

passages.text: A Pascha tamen usque Pentecosten nullus ieiunet, nisi sit preceptum <hi rend="bold">pro</hi><hi rend="bold"> publica</hi> pęnitentia; a die etiam natiuitatis Domini usque ad octauas Epiphanię <hi rend="spaced">idem custodiatur</hi>.
passages.en: From Easter until Pentecost however let no one fast, unless it be enjoined <hi rend="bold">for public</hi> penance; and from the day of the Lord's nativity until the octave of Epiphany <hi rend="spaced">let the same be observed</hi>.

passages.text: In omnibus festis et diebus ieiuniorum et diebus Quadragesimę et ab Aduentu Domini usque octo dies post <hi rend="bold">octauas</hi> Epiphanię et a Septuagesima usque quindecim dies post Pasca <hi rend="spaced">omnia</hi> iudicia <hi rend="bold">ferri et aquę</hi> et <hi rend="spaced">omne</hi> iusiurandum ex <hi rend="spaced">parte Dei</hi> prohibemus.
passages.en: On all feasts and fast days and the days of Lent, and from the Lord's Advent until eight days after the <hi rend="bold">octave</hi> of Epiphany, and from Septuagesima until fifteen days after Easter, we forbid <hi rend="spaced">all</hi> ordeals <hi rend="bold">of iron and water</hi> and <hi rend="spaced">every</hi> oath <hi rend="spaced">on God's part</hi>.

passages.text: [17, 1] Sapientes <hi rend="spaced">regni mei mecum</hi> decreuerunt celebrari festiuitatem sancti Eadƿardi <hi rend="bold">regis</hi> XV. kl. Aprilis et sancti Dunstani XIIII. kl. Iunii.
passages.en: [17, 1] The wise men <hi rend="spaced">of my kingdom with me</hi> have decreed that the feast of Saint Eadƿard the <hi rend="bold">king</hi> be celebrated on the 15th day before the Kalends of April and that of Saint Dunstan on the 14th day before the Kalends of June.

passages.text: [17, 2] In his diebus sit pax et securitas omnibus Christianis, et lis <hi rend="spaced">et contentio</hi> destruatur.
passages.en: [17, 2] On these days let there be peace and security for all Christians, and let strife <hi rend="spaced">and contention</hi> be put down.

passages.text: [17, 3] Et si aliquis <hi rend="spaced">debet alteri pecuniam aut aliquid aliud</hi>, reddat aut ante aut post <hi rend="spaced">in proximo</hi>.
passages.en: [17, 3] And if anyone <hi rend="spaced">owes another money or anything else</hi>, let him pay either before or after, <hi rend="spaced">at the nearest time</hi>.

passages.text: [19] Faciamus <hi rend="spaced">etiam, sicut nobis</hi> expedit: preparemus <hi rend="spaced">nosmet ipsos et tales nos exhibeamus</hi>, ut saltem ter in anno <hi rend="spaced">possimus</hi> communicari corporis et sanguinis Domini.
passages.en: [19] Let us <hi rend="spaced">also</hi> do <hi rend="spaced">as</hi> is expedient <hi rend="spaced">for us</hi>: let us prepare <hi rend="spaced">ourselves and show ourselves such</hi> that at least three times in the year we <hi rend="spaced">may be able</hi> to receive communion of the Lord's body and blood.

passages.text: [22] <hi rend="spaced">Debet etiam</hi> quisque Christianus discere ‘Pater noster’ et ‘Credo in <hi rend="spaced">Deum</hi>’,
passages.en: [22] <hi rend="spaced">Also</hi> every Christian <hi rend="spaced">ought</hi> to learn the ‘Pater noster’ and the ‘Credo in <hi rend="spaced">Deum</hi>’,

passages.text: [22, 1] quia per ‘<hi rend="spaced">Pater noster</hi>’ debet <hi rend="spaced">Deum</hi> orare et per ‘<hi rend="spaced">Credo</hi> <seg type="recension">(in Deum)</seg>’ fidem suam ostendere.
passages.en: [22, 1] because through the ‘<hi rend="spaced">Pater noster</hi>’ he ought to pray to <hi rend="spaced">God</hi> and through the ‘<hi rend="spaced">Credo</hi> <seg type="recension">(in Deum)</seg>’ show his faith.

passages.text: [22, 2] Christus ipse ‘Pater noster’ prius cantauit et postea discipulos suos docuit.
passages.en: [22, 2] Christ himself first sang the ‘Pater noster’ and afterwards taught it to his disciples.

passages.text: [22, 3] Per ‘<hi rend="spaced">Pater noster</hi>’ enim potest quisque promereri omne quod necessarium est in hoc sæculo et in futuro.
passages.en: [22, 3] For through the ‘<hi rend="spaced">Pater noster</hi>’ everyone can earn all that is needful in this world and in the next.

passages.text: [22, 4] Sed quomodo potest aliquis intimo corde Deum rogare, nisi habeat rectam credulitatem?
passages.en: [22, 4] But how can anyone pray to God with inmost heart unless he has right belief?

passages.text: [22, 5 <hi rend="italic">f</hi>.] <hi rend="spaced">Oportet ergo</hi>, ut post ‘Pater noster’ discat ‘<hi rend="spaced">Credo in Deum</hi>’, <hi rend="spaced">ut ostendat se Christi fidem habere</hi>. Et uere dico uobis: Non est perfecte Christianus <hi rend="spaced">nec est dignus</hi> corpus et sanguinem Domini accipere nec aliquem de baptismo leuare nec ad <hi rend="spaced">confirmandum</hi> ante episcopum ali<hi rend="spaced">quem tenere, et uere non est dignus, ut corpus eius inter corpora Christianorum sepeliatur</hi>, qui ista <hi rend="spaced">duo</hi> ignorat.
passages.en: [22, 5 <hi rend="italic">f</hi>.] <hi rend="spaced">It is fitting therefore</hi> that after the ‘Our Father’ he learn the ‘<hi rend="spaced">I believe in God</hi>’, <hi rend="spaced">so that he may show that he has the faith of Christ</hi>. And truly I say to you: he is not a perfect Christian <hi rend="spaced">nor is he worthy</hi> to receive the body and blood of the Lord, nor to lift anyone from baptism, nor for <hi rend="spaced">confirmation</hi> before the bishop to hold any<hi rend="spaced">one, and truly he is not worthy that his body be buried among the bodies of Christians</hi>, who does not know these <hi rend="spaced">two</hi>.

passages.text: Hęc est etiam institutio secularis, quam ego per consilium <seg type="recension">(et <hi rend="spaced">consensum</hi>)</seg> optimatum meorum seruare <hi rend="spaced">statui</hi> per totum regnum <hi rend="spaced">meum</hi>.
passages.en: This is also the secular ordinance which I, through the counsel <seg type="recension">(and <hi rend="spaced">consent</hi>)</seg> of my magnates, <hi rend="spaced">have resolved</hi> to keep throughout all <hi rend="spaced">my</hi> kingdom.

passages.text: Inprimis, ut iustę leges erigantur, et iniustę deprimantur et abiciantur;
passages.en: First, that just laws be raised up, and unjust ones be put down and cast away;

passages.text: recte leges diuiti et pauperi <hi rend="spaced">teneantur</hi>.
passages.en: that laws <hi rend="spaced">be held</hi> rightly for rich and poor.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="bold">iustitia</hi><hi rend="bold"> sit onerosa,</hi> consideret ille mensuram ad quem pertinebit tunc iusticia, sicut uult <hi rend="spaced">sibi</hi><hi rend="spaced"> prouideri a Deo</hi>, cui <hi rend="spaced">nos</hi><hi rend="spaced"> cotidie dicimus</hi>: ‘Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos <hi rend="spaced">dimittimus debitoribus nostris</hi>!’
passages.en: But if <hi rend="bold">justice be burdensome,</hi> let him to whom the justice will then pertain consider the measure, as he wishes <hi rend="spaced">to be provided for by God</hi>, to whom <hi rend="spaced">we daily say</hi>: ‘And forgive us our debts, as we also <hi rend="spaced">forgive our debtors</hi>!’

passages.text: Interdicimus etiam, ne pro parua re Christiani morti tradantur, <hi rend="bold">scilicet</hi><hi rend="bold"> pro latrocinio aut pro talibus rebus,</hi> sed alio modo <hi rend="spaced">corrigantur, propter</hi> <hi rend="spaced">alios</hi>, <hi rend="bold">ne culpę inulte</hi><hi rend="bold"> remaneant.</hi>
passages.en: We also forbid that for a small matter Christians be delivered to death, <hi rend="bold">namely for theft or for such things,</hi> but in another way let them <hi rend="spaced">be corrected, for the sake of</hi> <hi rend="spaced">others</hi>, <hi rend="bold">lest the offences remain unpunished.</hi>

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">prohibemus</hi>, ne Christiani <hi rend="spaced">gentibus</hi> extra <hi rend="spaced">hanc</hi> terram uenundentur nec in paganismo, ne anima <hi rend="spaced">Christiana</hi>, quam ipse Christus suo <hi rend="spaced">sanguine</hi> redemit, pereat.
passages.en: And we <hi rend="spaced">forbid</hi> that Christians be sold to <hi rend="spaced">heathens</hi> outside <hi rend="spaced">this</hi> land or into heathendom, lest a <hi rend="spaced">Christian</hi> soul, which Christ himself redeemed with his <hi rend="spaced">blood</hi>, perish.

passages.text: Incantatores et <hi rend="spaced">incantatrices</hi> et malefici aut <hi rend="spaced">apertę</hi> meretrices aut de regno <hi rend="spaced">nostro expellantur</hi> aut in terra <hi rend="spaced">male pereant</hi>, aut <hi rend="spaced">Deo et hominibus publice</hi> satisfaciant.
passages.en: Sorcerers and <hi rend="spaced">sorceresses</hi> and evil-doers or <hi rend="spaced">open</hi> whores either <hi rend="spaced">be expelled</hi> from <hi rend="spaced">our</hi> kingdom or <hi rend="spaced">perish miserably</hi> in the land, or make amends <hi rend="spaced">to God and men publicly</hi>.

passages.text: Interdicimus etiam omnem supersticionem paganorum,
passages.en: We also forbid all superstition of the heathens,

passages.text: uidelicet colere idola, solem, lunam, ignem, aquam, fontes, lapides, <hi rend="spaced">lignum</hi> <hi rend="spaced">frondosum</hi>, lignum uiride <hi rend="bold">aut aridum</hi> adorare, maleficia exercere, morthrum amare; <hi rend="bold">hęc </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(enim</hi><hi rend="bold">)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold"> omnia omni Christiano ex parte Dei prohibemus.</hi>
passages.en: namely to worship idols, sun, moon, fire, water, springs, stones, to adore a <hi rend="spaced">leafy</hi> <hi rend="spaced">tree</hi>, a green <hi rend="bold">or dry</hi> tree, to practise sorcery, to love murder; <hi rend="bold">all these things </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(indeed)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold"> we forbid to every Christian on God's behalf.</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Occulti</hi> homicidę, periuri, ordinum uiolatores <seg type="recension">(et)</seg> nuptiarum coniugatarum, <hi rend="spaced">quos</hi> <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi> ǽþbrece, aut <hi rend="bold">cito</hi> ad pęnitentiam <hi rend="spaced">currant</hi> aut <hi rend="bold">festinanter</hi> cum peccatis <hi rend="spaced">suis</hi> á regno nostro recedant.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Secret</hi> killers, perjurers, violators of holy orders <seg type="recension">(and)</seg> of married wedlock, <hi rend="spaced">whom</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ǽþbrece</hi> [adulterers], let them either <hi rend="bold">quickly</hi> <hi rend="spaced">run</hi> to penance or <hi rend="bold">hastily</hi> depart with <hi rend="spaced">their</hi> sins from our kingdom.

passages.text: Adulatores, mendaces, <hi rend="spaced">pauperum</hi> spoliatores et raptores <hi rend="spaced">cito</hi> iram Dei incurrant, nisi <hi rend="spaced">resipiscant et cessent et Deo</hi> satisfaciant.
passages.en: Flatterers, liars, despoilers <hi rend="spaced">of the poor</hi> and robbers shall <hi rend="spaced">quickly</hi> incur the wrath of God, unless they <hi rend="spaced">come to their senses and cease and to God</hi> make amends.

passages.text: Studeamus omnes omni instantia pacem et securitatem stabilire et <hi rend="spaced">stabilitatem</hi> monetę: sic pacem et securitatem, ut prosit <hi rend="spaced">pauperibus hominibus</hi> et obsit latronibus; sic stabilitatem monetę, ut una <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">teneatur</hi> et)</seg> uadat per totam terram <hi rend="spaced">Anglię</hi> sine falsitate, quam nullus deiciat.
passages.en: Let us all strive with all urgency to establish peace and security and <hi rend="spaced">stability</hi> of the coinage: peace and security such that it may benefit <hi rend="spaced">poor men</hi> and harm thieves; stability of the coinage such that one [coinage] <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">be held</hi> and)</seg> go throughout the whole land <hi rend="spaced">of England</hi> without falsity, which no one may reject.

passages.text: Et qui dehinc <hi rend="spaced">inuentus fuerit</hi> falsum fecisse, careat manibus, cum quibus falsum fecit, et nulla pecunia eas redimat, nec auro nec argento.
passages.en: And whoever henceforth <hi rend="spaced">shall be found</hi> to have made false [coin], let him lose the hands with which he made the false, and let him redeem them with no money, neither with gold nor with silver.

passages.text: Et si <hi rend="spaced">uicecomes</hi> <seg type="recension">(id est prępositus <hi rend="spaced">ciuitatis aut uillę</hi>)</seg> calumniatus fuerit, quod <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">falsator</hi>)</seg> per eius licentiam fecisset <hi rend="spaced">quod fecit</hi>, purget se triplici purgatione, <hi rend="bold">sacramenti aut igniti ferri </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(id</hi><hi rend="bold"> est ordel)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">,</hi> quod Angli <hi rend="spaced">nominant</hi> thrifealde lade <seg type="recension">(purgamine, q. A. <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> þrefeald l., <hi rend="bold">sa. aut i. f.,</hi> q. A. <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> <hi rend="bold">ordel)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">;</hi> et si ceciderit in purgatione, sustineat quod <hi rend="spaced">falsus monetarius</hi> sustinuit.
passages.en: And if the <hi rend="spaced">sheriff</hi> <seg type="recension">(that is, the reeve <hi rend="spaced">of the town or vill</hi>)</seg> is accused that <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">the counterfeiter</hi>)</seg> did <hi rend="spaced">what he did</hi> by his licence, let him clear himself with threefold purgation, <hi rend="bold">of oath or of hot iron </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(that is, ordeal)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">,</hi> which the English <hi rend="spaced">name</hi> <hi rend="italic">thrifealde lade</hi> [threefold exculpation] <seg type="recension">(with a purgation which the E. <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þrefeald l.</hi>, <hi rend="bold">of o. or of h. i.,</hi> which the E. <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">ordel</hi>)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">;</hi> and if he fails in the purgation, let him suffer what the <hi rend="spaced">false moneyer</hi> suffered.

passages.text: Mensurę et pondera <hi rend="spaced">per totum</hi> regnum <hi rend="spaced">Anglię</hi> ita corrigantur, ut sint recta <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">unita</hi>)</seg>.
passages.en: Measures and weights <hi rend="spaced">throughout the whole</hi> kingdom <hi rend="spaced">of England</hi> shall be so corrected that they be right <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">uniform</hi>)</seg>.

passages.text: Hę sunt consuetudines <hi rend="spaced">regis</hi>, quas habet super omnes homines in Westsexe: forisfacturam, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> mundbrece, hamsocne, <hi rend="spaced">hoc</hi> est inuasio in <hi rend="spaced">propria domo aut infra curiam</hi> causa <hi rend="spaced">alicuius mali</hi>, foresteal, <hi rend="spaced">quod nos possumus dicere contrastationem</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">causa mali</hi>; ferdƿite, <hi rend="spaced">quod nos possumus dicere dimissionem belli</hi>; hę sunt, <hi rend="spaced">inquam</hi>, consuetudines regis, nisi rex uelit aliquem <hi rend="spaced">honorare</hi>, dando ei <hi rend="spaced">quod sui iuris est</hi>.
passages.en: These are the rights of the <hi rend="spaced">king</hi> which he has over all men in Wessex: the forfeiture <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">mundbrece</hi> [breach of protection], <hi rend="italic">hamsocne</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">that</hi> is, attack <hi rend="spaced">in one's own house or within the courtyard</hi> for the sake <hi rend="spaced">of some evil</hi>, <hi rend="italic">foresteal</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which we can call 'obstruction'</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">for the sake of evil</hi>; <hi rend="italic">ferdƿite</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which we can call 'desertion of the army'</hi>; these are, <hi rend="spaced">I say</hi>, the king's rights, unless the king wishes to <hi rend="spaced">honour</hi> someone by giving him <hi rend="spaced">what is of his right</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">fecerit</hi> opus expulsi, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> útlages ƿeorc, uideat rex de pace.
passages.en: If anyone <hi rend="spaced">does</hi> the work of an outlaw, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">útlages ƿeorc</hi>, let the king see to [his] peace.

passages.text: Uerum si ipse habet alodium <seg type="recension">(bocland)</seg>, <seg type="recension">(suum)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">totum</hi> sit regis, cuiuscumque homo sit.
passages.en: But if he has allodial land <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="italic">bocland</hi>)</seg>, let <seg type="recension">(his)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">whole</hi> be the king's, whosesoever man he be.

passages.text: Et qui exulem <seg type="recension">(quem Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> <hi rend="bold">utlaga</hi>)</seg> pauerit post ex<hi rend="spaced">pulsionem, quod Angli dicunt</hi> fede oþþe fermie, det regi <hi rend="spaced">centum solidos</hi>, nisi se purgauerit, quod illum nescisset expulsum <hi rend="bold">clamatum</hi><hi rend="bold">, quod Angli dicunt gecydne</hi><hi rend="bold"> utlage.</hi>
passages.en: And whoever has fed an exile <seg type="recension">(whom the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">utlaga</hi></hi>)</seg> after the ex<hi rend="spaced">pulsion, which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">fede oþþe fermie</hi> [feeds or harbours], let him give the king <hi rend="spaced">a hundred shillings</hi>, unless he clears himself [by oath] that he did not know him [to be] expelled <hi rend="bold">[and] proclaimed, which the English call <hi rend="italic">gecydne utlage</hi> [declared outlaw].</hi>

passages.text: In lege Mercia rex habet easdem <hi rend="spaced">consuetudines</hi>.
passages.en: In the Mercian law the king has the same <hi rend="spaced">rights</hi>.

passages.text: In lege autem Danorum habet rex has <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">consuetudines</hi>)</seg>: uiolationem <hi rend="bold">monetę,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> <hi rend="bold">feohƿíte,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">dimissionem belli</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli</hi><hi rend="spaced"> dicunt</hi> ferdƿite, fractionem pacis, <hi rend="spaced">quod dicunt</hi> griðbrece, inuasionem in domo uel in <hi rend="spaced">curia, quod dicunt hamsocne</hi>, nisi <hi rend="spaced">rex uelit</hi> <hi rend="spaced">dare quod suum est</hi>.
passages.en: But in the law of the Danes the king has these <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">rights</hi>)</seg>: violation <hi rend="bold">of the coinage,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">feohƿíte</hi>,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">desertion of the army</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ferdƿite</hi>, breach of the peace, <hi rend="spaced">which they call</hi> <hi rend="italic">griðbrece</hi>, attack in a house or in a <hi rend="spaced">courtyard, which they call <hi rend="italic">hamsocne</hi></hi>, unless <hi rend="spaced">the king wishes</hi> <hi rend="spaced">to give what is his</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis iniustas leges adinuerit et iudicauerit, aut causa odii aut adquisitionis pecunię, sit reus regi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> sol. in lege Anglorum, nisi iuramento affirmauerit, se rectius <hi rend="spaced">iudicare</hi> nescisse, et postea careat <hi rend="spaced">liberalitate</hi> sua, nisi eam á rege redimat ad <hi rend="spaced">uelle regis</hi>.
passages.en: If anyone devises unjust laws and judges [by them], either for the sake of hatred or of acquiring money, let him be liable to the king for <hi rend="bold">40</hi> shillings in the law of the English, unless he affirms by oath that he did not know how <hi rend="spaced">to judge</hi> more rightly, and afterwards let him lose his <hi rend="spaced">noble rank</hi>, unless he redeem it from the king at <hi rend="spaced">the king's will</hi>.

passages.text: In lege Danorum erit reus forisfacturę, <hi rend="spaced">quam</hi> <hi rend="bold">Dani</hi> <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> lahslit . . .
passages.en: In the law of the Danes he shall be liable for the forfeiture <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> <hi rend="bold">the Danes</hi> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> [fine for breach of law] . . .

passages.text: In lege eorum liberalis hominis lahslit uocant X dimidię marcę, hoc est V marcę; hominis alodium <seg type="recension">(bocland)</seg> habentis sex dimidię marcę, hoc est tres marcę; uillani lahslit, quem Angli uocant ceorlman XII orę.
passages.en: In their law they call the <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> [fine for breach of law] of a free man of rank (thegn) ten half-marks, that is five marks; of a man having allodial land <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="italic">bocland</hi>)</seg> six half-marks, that is three marks; the <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> of a villein, whom the English call <hi rend="italic">ceorlman</hi>, twelve ores.

passages.text: Qui expulsum pauerit aut <hi rend="spaced">detinuerit pacifice</hi>, quem Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> friðleasne man, reddat regi, sicut lex est, <hi rend="spaced">plenam emendationem</hi>, <hi rend="bold">et illi</hi><hi rend="bold"> qui</hi><hi rend="bold"> expulsum expulit despectum suum, si ita iustum</hi><hi rend="bold"> est.</hi>
passages.en: Whoever feeds an expelled man or <hi rend="spaced">keeps [him] peaceably</hi>, whom the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">friðleasne man</hi> [man without peace], let him pay the king, as the law is, <hi rend="spaced">full compensation</hi>, <hi rend="bold">and to him who expelled the expelled man his contempt-fine, if that is just.</hi>

passages.text: Qui rectum iudicium et iustam legem abnegat, sit forisfactus ei cui <hi rend="spaced">iustum est</hi>: si regi, det illi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> solidos, si comiti <hi rend="bold">XX</hi> solidos, si hundredo <hi rend="bold">X</hi> solidos, si contra omnes hos, <hi rend="spaced">omnibus reddat</hi>.
passages.en: Whoever refuses right judgment and just law, let him be forfeit to the one to whom <hi rend="spaced">it is due</hi>: if to the king, let him give him <hi rend="bold">40</hi> shillings, if to the earl <hi rend="bold">20</hi> shillings, if to the hundred <hi rend="bold">10</hi> shillings, if against all these, <hi rend="spaced">let him pay to all</hi>.

passages.text: Per legem Danorum lahslit reddat.
passages.en: By the law of the Danes let him pay <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis alium iniuste accusauerit, <hi rend="spaced">ita ut accusatus perditurus sit propter delationem</hi> accusantis pecuniam aut <hi rend="bold">uitam,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">et accusatus se</hi> inde purgauerit, <hi rend="spaced">delator</hi> sit reus linguę suę, nisi <hi rend="spaced">persoluat delatum</hi> secundum pretium suum, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> be his ƿere.
passages.en: If anyone accuses another unjustly, <hi rend="spaced">so that the accused would lose through the denunciation</hi> of the accuser money or <hi rend="bold">life,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and the accused</hi> clears <hi rend="spaced">himself</hi> of it, let the <hi rend="spaced">denouncer</hi> be liable for his tongue, unless he <hi rend="spaced">pays for the denounced</hi> according to his own price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">be his ƿere</hi> [by his wergeld].

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Constituantur</hi> <hi rend="bold">popularia</hi> placita, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> hundred, sicut <hi rend="bold">iustum est et</hi><hi rend="bold"> ante hoc</hi><hi rend="bold"> factum est,</hi> super forisfacturam <hi rend="bold">quam lex docet;</hi> et nemo requirat regem, nisi non possit habere rectitudinem in hundredo suo.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Let</hi> <hi rend="bold">popular</hi> courts <hi rend="spaced">be established</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">hundred</hi>, as <hi rend="bold">is just and has been done before this,</hi> under the forfeiture <hi rend="bold">which the law teaches;</hi> and let no one apply to the king unless he cannot obtain right in his hundred.

passages.text: Ciuilia placita ter in anno teneantur, et comitatus bis in anno <hi rend="spaced">congregetur</hi>, nisi plus <hi rend="bold">necesse</hi> sit.
passages.en: Let civil courts be held three times a year, and the shire (court) <hi rend="spaced">be assembled</hi> twice a year, unless more be <hi rend="bold">necessary</hi>.

passages.text: Et in illo <hi rend="spaced">comitatu</hi> sint episcopus et comes, qui <hi rend="spaced">ostendant</hi> populo et iusticias Dei et rectitudines saeculi.
passages.en: And at that <hi rend="spaced">shire court</hi> let there be the bishop and the earl, who are to <hi rend="spaced">show</hi> the people both the justices of God and the rights of the world.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> náme nec infra comitatum nec extra, antequam ter iusticiam in hundredo requirat. Nullus accipiat pro aliqua forisfactura quicquam quod Angli
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">náme</hi> [distraint] neither within the shire nor outside, before he has three times sought justice in the hundred. Let no one take for any forfeiture anything which the English

passages.text: Quodsi uice tertia rectum habere non poterit, eat ad comitatum <hi rend="bold">et ostendat, se iam tercio</hi><hi rend="bold"> hundredum adiisse, rectum</hi><hi rend="bold"> requisisse et habere non potuisse;</hi> tunc comitatus statuat illi diem, <hi rend="bold">in quo qui calumniatur</hi><hi rend="bold"> faciat</hi><hi rend="bold"> rectum.</hi>
passages.en: But if the third time he cannot have right, let him go to the shire (court) <hi rend="bold">and show that he has now gone to the hundred three times, sought right and could not have it;</hi> then let the shire appoint him a day, <hi rend="bold">on which he who is accused shall do right.</hi>

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">dies statutus</hi> fractus fuerit, accepta licentia a comitatu in <hi rend="spaced">eundo</hi> et in redeundo, ut possit <hi rend="bold">accipere náme,</hi> quousque habeat sua.
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">the appointed day</hi> is broken, leave having been received from the shire for <hi rend="spaced">going</hi> and returning, so that he may <hi rend="bold">take <hi rend="italic">náme</hi>,</hi> until he has his own.

passages.text: Constituimus etiam, ut omnis liber homo, qui uoluerit esse dignus <hi rend="spaced">purgatione et libertate</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">quod</hi> <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> lade þurþe ⁊ þeres þurþe, sit in hundredo et in <hi rend="bold">plegio;</hi> aliter si <hi rend="bold">occisus</hi> fuerit, postquam fuerit duodennis, non erit ulla liberalitate dignus.
passages.en: We also establish that every free man who wishes to be worthy of <hi rend="spaced">exculpation and freedom</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">lade þurþe ⁊ þeres þurþe</hi> [worthy of exculpation and of wergeld], be in a hundred and in <hi rend="bold">pledge;</hi> otherwise, if he is <hi rend="bold">slain</hi> after he is twelve years old, he shall be worthy of no freeman's status.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Hoc quoque dicimus</hi> et de iis qui domum et <hi rend="spaced">terram</hi> habent et de iis qui <hi rend="spaced">non</hi>, sed <hi rend="spaced">seruiunt</hi> aliis, quos Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> husfæst ⁊ folgæres, ut omnes sint in hundredo et sub plegio, qui eos <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">teneat</hi>)</seg> ad iusticiam habeat, <hi rend="bold">si aliquando calumniantur</hi><hi rend="bold"> de aliqua</hi><hi rend="bold"> re.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">This too we say</hi> both of those who have house and <hi rend="spaced">land</hi> and of those who <hi rend="spaced">do not</hi>, but <hi rend="spaced">serve</hi> others, whom the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">husfæst ⁊ folgæres</hi> [householders and followers], that all be in a hundred and under pledge, which shall have <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">hold</hi>)</seg> them to justice, <hi rend="bold">if at any time they are accused of any matter.</hi>

passages.text: Multi fortes homines uolunt <hi rend="spaced">cum</hi> <hi rend="spaced">ingenio</hi> defendere in pla<hi rend="spaced">citis suos subiectos</hi>, quo leuius illis posse uidetur, pro seruis aut pro liberis; sed nos huic iniusticie consentire nolumus.
passages.en: Many powerful men wish <hi rend="spaced">with</hi> <hi rend="spaced">cunning</hi> to defend in the cou<hi rend="spaced">rts their dependants</hi>, in whatever way seems to them easier to be able, for slaves or for free men; but we do not wish to consent to this injustice.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Propterea</hi> pręcipimus, ut omnis homo ultra <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">ętatem</hi>)</seg> duodecim annorum faciat sacramentum, quod nec latro uult esse nec latroni consentire.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Therefore</hi> we command that every man over <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">the age</hi>)</seg> of twelve years take an oath that he will neither be a thief nor be an accomplice of a thief.

passages.text: Si sit autem quisquam fidelis homo, qui <hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi> non fuerit calumniatus <hi rend="spaced">de aliqua turpi</hi> re, et cui iuramentum non fregerit in ore nec iudicium <hi rend="bold">ferri uel aquę,</hi> quod <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> þa<hi rend="italic">m</hi> þe ue bærst ne aþ ne ordel, <hi rend="spaced">iste talis, si aliquando calumniatus fuerit, purget se simplici</hi> purgatione.
passages.en: But if there is any trustworthy man, who has not <hi rend="spaced">rightly</hi> been accused <hi rend="spaced">of any shameful</hi> matter, and for whom neither the oath has broken in his mouth nor the ordeal <hi rend="bold">of iron or water,</hi> which <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> þa<hi rend="italic">m</hi> þe ue bærst ne aþ ne ordel [for whom neither oath nor ordeal has failed], <hi rend="spaced">such a one, if at any time he is accused, let him clear himself with simple</hi> purgation.

passages.text: Infideli autem homini eligatur iuramentum, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> anfealdne að, in hundredo, et triplex iuramentum, sicut <hi rend="spaced">conuenit curię illi ad quam pertinet</hi>; aut uadat ad iudicium.
passages.en: But for an untrustworthy man let a [selected] oath be chosen, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">anfealdne að</hi> [single oath], in the hundred, and a threefold oath, as <hi rend="spaced">befits that court to which he belongs</hi>; or let him go to the ordeal.

passages.text: Qui autem conquirere debet simplicem purgationem, simplici sacramento <hi rend="spaced">hoc faciat</hi>, <hi rend="bold">hoc est accipiat duos, et sit ipse tertius et sic iurando conquirat.</hi> <hi rend="bold">Triplex</hi><hi rend="bold"> uero</hi><hi rend="bold"> iuramentum sic conquiratur: accipiat quinque et sit</hi><hi rend="bold"> ipse sextus et sic iurando adquirat triplex iudicium aut triplex iuramentum.</hi>
passages.en: But whoever must obtain simple purgation, let him <hi rend="spaced">do this</hi> with a simple oath, <hi rend="bold">that is, let him take two, and be himself the third, and so obtain it by swearing.</hi> <hi rend="bold">But a threefold oath is to be obtained thus: let him take five and be himself the sixth, and so by swearing acquire threefold ordeal or threefold oath.</hi>

passages.text: Si liberalis homo, id est þegen, habet fidelem hominem, <hi rend="spaced">qui pro eo possit iurare praeiuramentum</hi> <seg type="recension">(id est foraþ)</seg>, ita sit; si autem non habet, ipsemet <hi rend="spaced">iuret</hi>.
passages.en: If a free man of rank (thegn), that is <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi>, has a trustworthy man <hi rend="spaced">who can swear the fore-oath for him</hi> <seg type="recension">(that is <hi rend="italic">foraþ</hi>)</seg>, so be it; but if he does not have one, let him <hi rend="spaced">swear</hi> himself.

passages.text: Nec ei perdonetur aliquod preiuramentum.
passages.en: Nor shall any fore-oath be remitted to him.

passages.text: <hi rend="bold">Si latrocinium inuenitur in manu uel</hi><hi rend="bold"> in potestate alicuius, qui se non poterit excusare, si uult</hi> warantem nominare, nullo modo ei liceat, nisi habeat <hi rend="bold">duos</hi> idoneos testes, qui <hi rend="spaced">fuerint uidentes et audientes</hi>, unde sibi uenit quod <hi rend="spaced">in manu sua uel in potestate</hi> captum est.
passages.en: <hi rend="bold">If stolen goods are found in the hand or in the power of anyone who cannot excuse himself, if he wishes</hi> to name a warrantor, it shall in no way be allowed him, unless he has <hi rend="bold">two</hi> suitable witnesses who <hi rend="spaced">were seeing and hearing</hi> whence there came to him what was taken <hi rend="spaced">in his hand or in his power</hi>.

passages.text: Et ostendant testes hoc <hi rend="spaced">per sacramentum</hi>, quod iuste sibi sunt testes et <hi rend="spaced">fideles</hi>, sicut uidentes et audientes, in fide Dei et per fidem <hi rend="spaced">domini sui</hi>, quod iuste illud adquisiuit.
passages.en: And let the witnesses show this <hi rend="spaced">by oath</hi>, that they are rightly witnesses for him and <hi rend="spaced">trustworthy</hi>, as seeing and hearing, in the faith of God and by the faith <hi rend="spaced">of their lord</hi>, that he acquired it rightly.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Uolumus</hi> etiam, ut nullus emat aliquid ultra quattuor dena<hi rend="spaced">riorum</hi><hi rend="spaced"> ualens</hi>, nec rem uiuam nec <hi rend="spaced">mortuam</hi> nec iacentem, sine quattuor idoneis testibus, nec infra burgum nec <hi rend="spaced">extra</hi>.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">We wish</hi> also that no one buy anything above four pe<hi rend="spaced">nce in value</hi>, neither a living thing nor a <hi rend="spaced">dead</hi> one nor a lying one, without four suitable witnesses, neither within a borough nor <hi rend="spaced">outside</hi>.

passages.text: Et si non <hi rend="spaced">tot nec tales</hi> testes habuerit, et aliquid tale <hi rend="spaced">in manu</hi> uel <hi rend="spaced">potestate eius</hi> inuentum fuerit, et ipse warantem <hi rend="spaced">uoluerit uocare</hi>, non ei ualeat <hi rend="spaced">neque</hi> liceat, sed reddatur calumnianti quod suum est — <hi rend="bold">aut ualens</hi> — et insuper iterum tantum ualens, et forisfacturam qui eam <hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi> habere debet.
passages.en: And if he does not have <hi rend="spaced">so many nor such</hi> witnesses, and some such thing is found <hi rend="spaced">in the hand</hi> or <hi rend="spaced">his power</hi>, and he <hi rend="spaced">wishes to vouch</hi> a warrantor, it shall not avail him <hi rend="spaced">nor</hi> be allowed, but let what is his be returned to the claimant — <hi rend="bold">or its value</hi> — and besides again as much in value, and the forfeiture [to him] who <hi rend="spaced">rightly</hi> ought to have it.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">tales testes</hi> habuerit, quales supra diximus, warantem uocet; <hi rend="bold">et ille uocatus uocet</hi><hi rend="bold"> alium, si potest, et tertius adhuc tertium</hi><hi rend="bold"> uocet, si potest;</hi> et tertius suum faciet, <hi rend="spaced">si ualet; quodsi non ualet</hi>, reddatur ei, qui iuste habere debet.
passages.en: But if he has <hi rend="spaced">such witnesses</hi> as we said above, let him vouch the warrantor; <hi rend="bold">and let the one vouched vouch another, if he can, and the third further vouch a third, if he can;</hi> and the third shall make it his own, <hi rend="spaced">if he is able; but if he is not able</hi>, let it be returned to him who rightly ought to have it.

passages.text: Nobis <hi rend="spaced">tamen</hi> iniustum uidetur, quod aliquis debeat sibi <hi rend="spaced">iurando</hi> uindicare, <hi rend="spaced">quod iuste suum est</hi>, ubi testes sunt, et saltem ante sex menses, postquam furto ablatum est <hi rend="spaced">quod quęrit</hi>.
passages.en: To us <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> it seems unjust that anyone should claim for himself <hi rend="spaced">by swearing</hi> <hi rend="spaced">what is rightly his</hi>, where there are witnesses, and at least before six months after <hi rend="spaced">what he seeks</hi> was taken away by theft.

passages.text: Qui sepe calumniatus est de furto et <hi rend="bold">hundredum</hi> uocatus ter declinet: inueniantur de <hi rend="bold">hundredo</hi> qui eum adeant; et inueniat, si potest, adhuc plegios.
passages.en: Whoever has often been accused of theft and, summoned [to] the <hi rend="bold">hundred</hi>, three times declines: let men be found from the <hi rend="bold">hundred</hi> who shall go to him; and let him find, if he can, sureties still.

passages.text: Quodsi non <hi rend="spaced">potuerit aut noluerit</hi>, capiatur aut uiuus aut mortuus et omnia quę habet.
passages.en: But if he <hi rend="spaced">could not or would not</hi>, let him be taken either alive or dead, and all that he has.

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">inprimis</hi> reddatur calumnianti de rebus latronis, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> his ceapgeld; et quod remanet <hi rend="spaced">diuidatur</hi> per medium inter hundredum et dominum <hi rend="spaced">latronis</hi>.
passages.en: And <hi rend="spaced">first</hi> let there be returned to the claimant from the thief's goods [what] <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">his ceapgeld</hi> [his purchase-price]; and what remains <hi rend="spaced">let be divided</hi> in half between the hundred and the lord <hi rend="spaced">of the thief</hi>.

passages.text: Si autem parens <hi rend="spaced">illius latronis aut aliquis alius</hi> contradixerit adire <hi rend="spaced">illum</hi> latronem, sicut <hi rend="spaced">diximus</hi>, det regi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> solidos.
passages.en: But if a kinsman <hi rend="spaced">of that thief or anyone else</hi> refuses to go against <hi rend="spaced">that</hi> thief, as <hi rend="spaced">we have said</hi>, let him give the king <hi rend="bold">40</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Publicus latro et traditor proprii domini, <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli uocant</hi> hlaford<hi rend="bold">spice</hi>, quicquid re<hi rend="spaced">quisierint, nusquam uitam inueueniant</hi>.
passages.en: A public thief and betrayer of his own lord, <hi rend="spaced">whom the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">hlaford</hi><hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">spice</hi></hi> [lord-traitor], whatever they re<hi rend="spaced">quest, let them nowhere find life</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis in placitis per contrarias calumnias uult defendere se ipsum aut hominem suum, pro nichilo habeantur illę calumnię, sed <hi rend="spaced">respondeat calumnianti se</hi>, sicut hundred iudicauerit.
passages.en: If anyone in the courts wishes to defend himself or his man by counter-accusations, let those accusations be held as nothing, but <hi rend="spaced">let him answer the one accusing him</hi>, as the <hi rend="italic">hundred</hi> shall judge.

passages.text: Nemo teneat aliquem hominem diutius <hi rend="spaced">tribus noctibus</hi>, nisi <hi rend="spaced">dominus eius</hi>, cui prius seruiuit, eum commendauerit. <hi rend="bold">Quodsi aliter fecerit, persoluat priori</hi><hi rend="bold"> domino despectum eius et regi forisfacturam suam.</hi>
passages.en: Let no one keep any man longer than <hi rend="spaced">three nights</hi>, unless <hi rend="spaced">his lord</hi>, whom he served before, has commended him. <hi rend="bold">But if he does otherwise, let him pay the former lord his contempt-fine and the king his forfeiture.</hi>

passages.text: Nullus repellat a se seruientem suum, antequam sit purgatus de omni calumnia, unde fuit prius calumniatus.
passages.en: Let no one put away from himself his servant before he is cleared of every accusation of which he was previously accused.

passages.text: Si cui latro occurrerit, et sine clamore sponte illum abire permiserit, soluat latronem, <hi rend="bold">cui iustum est,</hi> prętio eiusdem latronis aut purget se pleno iuramento, quod eundem <hi rend="spaced">nesciuit esse latronem</hi>.
passages.en: If a thief encounters anyone, and he willingly lets him go without hue and cry, let him pay for the thief, <hi rend="bold">to whom it is due,</hi> at the price of the same thief, or let him clear himself with a full oath that he <hi rend="spaced">did not know him to be a thief</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis est infidelis hundredo suo et sepe est calumniatus, si <hi rend="spaced">simul uno die tribus calumniis</hi> proclamatus fuerit, triplici iudicio <hi rend="spaced">se purget</hi>.
passages.en: If anyone is untrustworthy to his hundred and is often accused, if he is charged <hi rend="spaced">together on one day with three accusations</hi>, let him <hi rend="spaced">clear himself</hi> by threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Quodsi dominus eius dixerit, quia <hi rend="spaced">nunquam illi</hi> fregerit iuramentum <seg type="recension">(sacramentum)</seg> nec iudicium, nec prętium latrocinii persoluit, tunc ille dominus accipiat secum duos fideles et hoc <hi rend="spaced">ita esse sacramento affirmet</hi>, nisi talem prępositum habeat, qui dignus sit hoc idem <hi rend="spaced">pro eo facere</hi>.
passages.en: But if his lord says that <hi rend="spaced">never for him</hi> has oath <seg type="recension">(sworn oath)</seg> or ordeal broken, nor has he paid the price of theft, then let that lord take with him two trustworthy men and <hi rend="spaced">affirm by oath that it is so</hi>, unless he has such a reeve as is worthy <hi rend="spaced">to do this same for him</hi>.

passages.text: Si sacramentum bene processerit, <hi rend="spaced">ille calumniatus eligat</hi>, quid horum uoluerit, aut simplex iudicium aut sacramentum <hi rend="bold">XX</hi><hi rend="bold"> solidorum</hi> in tribus hundredis, ultra XXXta denarios.
passages.en: If the oath goes well, let <hi rend="spaced">the accused choose</hi> which of these he wishes, either simple ordeal or an oath <hi rend="bold">of 20 shillings</hi> in three hundreds, above 30 pence.

passages.text: Quodsi non <hi rend="spaced">audent</hi> sacramentum facere, eat ad triplex iudicium.
passages.en: But if they <hi rend="spaced">dare</hi> not make the oath, let him go to the threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Ita autem <hi rend="spaced">adquiratur</hi> illud triplex iudicium <seg type="recension">(quod <hi rend="spaced">Angli dicunt</hi> ‘<hi rend="bold">ofræce</hi> <hi rend="italic">þæt</hi> ordel')</seg>: accipiat secum quinque et sit ipse sextus; <hi rend="spaced">ita enim</hi> conquiritur triplex iudicium.
passages.en: Thus <hi rend="spaced">is to be obtained</hi> that threefold ordeal <seg type="recension">(which <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> ‘<hi rend="bold">ofræce</hi> <hi rend="italic">þæt</hi> ordel')</seg>: let him take with him five and be himself the sixth; <hi rend="spaced">for thus</hi> is threefold ordeal obtained.
