passages.text: Quodsi reus fuerit et in iudicio <hi rend="spaced">ceciderit</hi>, prima uice ante alia reddat <hi rend="spaced">calumniantibus</hi> dupliciter sua, et dominis illorum <hi rend="spaced">pretium eorum</hi>, et postea <hi rend="spaced">inueniant</hi> fideiussores, quod deinde <hi rend="spaced">cessabunt</hi>.
passages.en: But if he is guilty and <hi rend="spaced">fails</hi> in the ordeal, the first time let him before other things repay <hi rend="spaced">the accusers</hi> double what is theirs, and to their lords <hi rend="spaced">their price</hi>, and afterwards let them <hi rend="spaced">find</hi> sureties that they will thenceforth <hi rend="spaced">desist</hi>.

passages.text: Si secundo <hi rend="spaced">ceciderint</hi>, abscidantur illis manus aut pedes <hi rend="spaced">aut utrumque, si culpa tanta</hi> fuerit.
passages.en: If they <hi rend="spaced">fail</hi> a second time, let their hands or feet be cut off, <hi rend="spaced">or both, if the guilt be so great</hi>.

passages.text: Quodsi adhuc maiora fecerit, eruantur sibi oculi, et auferatur sibi nasus cum labro et aures aut corium capitis cum capillis, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> <hi rend="bold">behætian</hi>; sic possunt <hi rend="spaced">latrones</hi> corrigi et <hi rend="spaced">animę</hi> saluari.
passages.en: But if he has done still greater things, let his eyes be put out, and his nose be taken off with the lip, and the ears, or the skin of the head with the hair, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">behætian</hi></hi> [to scalp]; thus can <hi rend="spaced">thieves</hi> be corrected and <hi rend="spaced">souls</hi> saved.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">calumniatus euaserit</hi> et iudicium declinauerit, fideiussores <hi rend="spaced">reddant calumnianti</hi> quod á <hi rend="spaced">latrone</hi> exegit, et regi prętium <hi rend="spaced">latronis</hi> aut illi qui habet <hi rend="bold">sacę</hi><hi rend="bold"> et socne.</hi>
passages.en: But if the <hi rend="spaced">accused escapes</hi> and avoids the ordeal, the sureties are to <hi rend="spaced">pay back to the accuser</hi> what he claimed from the <hi rend="spaced">thief</hi>, and to the king the price of the <hi rend="spaced">thief</hi>, or to him who has <hi rend="bold">sake and soke.</hi>

passages.text: Quodsi dominus latronis inculpatus fuerit, quasi sponte illum ire <hi rend="spaced">permiserit</hi>, acceptis quinque <hi rend="spaced">fidelibus hominibus</hi> purget se, <hi rend="spaced">si potest</hi>.
passages.en: But if the lord of the thief is accused, as though he willingly <hi rend="spaced">let</hi> him go, taking five <hi rend="spaced">trustworthy men</hi> let him clear himself, <hi rend="spaced">if he can</hi>.

passages.text: Si se purgauerit, illi detur <hi rend="spaced">prętium latronis, id est</hi> ƿere.
passages.en: If he clears himself, let there be given to him the <hi rend="spaced">price of the thief, that is,</hi> the <hi rend="italic">ƿere</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">purgare</hi> se non poterit, rex habeat illud prętium; et latro habeatur <hi rend="spaced">exul et reus</hi> ab omni populo.
passages.en: If he cannot <hi rend="spaced">clear</hi> himself, let the king have that price; and let the thief be held <hi rend="spaced">an outlaw and guilty</hi> by all the people.

passages.text: Omnis dominus habeat familiam suam in proprio plegio <seg type="recension">(suo)</seg>, ut, si aliquis <hi rend="spaced">illorum</hi> calumniatus fuerit, respondeat hundredo, in quo calumniatus est, sicut iustum sit.
passages.en: Every lord is to have his household in his own <seg type="recension">(his)</seg> pledge, so that, if any <hi rend="spaced">of them</hi> is accused, he answers to the <hi rend="italic">hundred</hi> in which he is accused, as is right.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">post</hi> calumniam euaserit, dominus soluat eius ƿere regi, <hi rend="bold">et plegii quod calumniatus est. Si autem infra annum et unum diem dominus eius illum capere</hi><hi rend="bold"> poterit, recipiat hoc quod pro eo dedit.</hi>
passages.en: If he escapes <hi rend="spaced">after</hi> the accusation, the lord is to pay his <hi rend="italic">ƿere</hi> to the king, <hi rend="bold">and to the pledges what he was accused of. But if within a year and a day his lord can catch him, he is to get back what he gave for him.</hi>

passages.text: Et si ipse dominus calumniatus fuerit, quod eum sponte fugere permiserit, <hi rend="bold">si ille est</hi><hi rend="bold"> liberalis,</hi> id <hi rend="spaced">est þegen</hi>, acceptis quinque similibus purget se.
passages.en: And if the lord himself is accused of having let him flee willingly, <hi rend="bold">if he is a free man of rank,</hi> that <hi rend="spaced">is a <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi></hi> [thegn], taking five of his like let him clear himself.

passages.text: Si non <hi rend="spaced">poterit</hi> purgare se, persoluat regi ƿere suum; et homo sit exul <hi rend="spaced">ab omnibus</hi>.
passages.en: If he <hi rend="spaced">cannot</hi> clear himself, let him pay the king his <hi rend="italic">ƿere</hi>; and the man is to be an outlaw <hi rend="spaced">from all</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">seruus ceciderit</hi> in iudicio <hi rend="bold">ferri aut</hi><hi rend="bold"> aquę,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">criminis</hi> signum prima uice fiet ei.
passages.en: If a <hi rend="spaced">slave fails</hi> in the ordeal <hi rend="bold">of iron or water,</hi> a mark <hi rend="spaced">of crime</hi> is to be made on him the first time.

passages.text: Si secundo ceciderit, nichil aliud <hi rend="spaced">emendationis</hi> accipiatur, nisi ut ei caput <hi rend="spaced">abscidatur</hi>.
passages.en: If he fails a second time, let nothing else be accepted <hi rend="spaced">by way of amends</hi>, except that his head <hi rend="spaced">be cut off</hi>.

passages.text: Qui omni populo infidelis est, prępositus regis ponat eum sub fideiussoribus, ut custodiant illum ad iusticiam.
passages.en: Whoever is untrustworthy to all the people, the king's reeve is to put him under sureties, so that they keep him to justice.

passages.text: Et si non <hi rend="spaced">potest</hi> habere plegios, occidatur et in loco latronum sepeliatur.
passages.en: And if he <hi rend="spaced">cannot</hi> have pledges, let him be killed and buried in the place of thieves.

passages.text: Quod si forte aliquis eum ui defendere uoluerit, habeat eandem legem.
passages.en: But if perhaps anyone wishes to defend him by force, let him have the same law.

passages.text: Et qui hec supersederit et ista facere noluerit, sicut nos omnes simul <hi rend="spaced">condiximus</hi>, det regi <hi rend="bold">quadraginta</hi> solidos.
passages.en: And whoever neglects these things and will not do them, as we all together <hi rend="spaced">agreed</hi>, let him give the king <hi rend="bold">forty</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Et sit inter <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">omnes</hi>)</seg> ciuitates una lex et una purgatio.
passages.en: And let there be among <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">all</hi>)</seg> the towns one law and one purgation.

passages.text: Si aduena aut peregrinus, qui de longinquo uenit, sit tribulatus pro penuria amicorum, ut non possit habere plegios, ad primam calumniam, tunc subeat captionem <hi rend="bold">regis</hi> et ibi expectet, quoad usque uadat ad iudicium <hi rend="bold">ferri aut</hi><hi rend="bold"> aquę</hi> illicque inueniat quod potest.
passages.en: If a stranger or foreigner, who comes from afar, is in difficulty for lack of friends, so that he cannot have pledges, at the first accusation, then let him undergo the <hi rend="bold">king's</hi> custody and wait there until he goes to the ordeal <hi rend="bold">of iron or water</hi> and there find what he can.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Certe dico uobis</hi>, si quis extraneo aut peregrino de longe uenienti <hi rend="spaced">aliud</hi> iudicium iudicauerit, sibi ipsi nocet.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Truly I tell you</hi>, if anyone judges a <hi rend="spaced">different</hi> judgement for a stranger or foreigner coming from afar, he harms himself.

passages.text: Si quis periurium fecerit <hi rend="bold">super textum euangelil aut</hi> super reliquias sanctorum et uictus fuerit, <hi rend="spaced">quod iniuste iurauerit</hi>, careat <hi rend="spaced">manibus</hi> aut det dimidium prętii sui ipsius; et hoc diuidatur inter episcopum et dominum ipsius hominis.
passages.en: If anyone commits perjury <hi rend="bold">on the text of the Gospel or</hi> on the relics of the saints and is convicted <hi rend="spaced">of having sworn unjustly</hi>, let him lose his <hi rend="spaced">hands</hi> or give half of his own price; and this is to be divided between the bishop and the lord of that man.

passages.text: Et post hoc non sit dignus iuramenti, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> aðes þyrðe, nisi altius Deo satisfaciat et fideiussores inueniat, quod amplius cessauerit.
passages.en: And after this let him not be worthy of an oath, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">aðes þyrðe</hi>, unless he makes satisfaction to God more deeply and finds sureties that he will cease henceforth.

passages.text: Qui uero steterit in falso testimonio et uictus fuerit, <hi rend="spaced">quod</hi> ita sit, non sit amplius dignus stare aut <hi rend="spaced">portare testimonium</hi>, <hi rend="bold">quia legalitatem suam perdidit</hi>, et ideo persoluat regi aut domino terrę <hi rend="bold">X solidos,</hi> quod <hi rend="bold">Dani</hi> <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> halsfang.
passages.en: But whoever stands in false witness and is convicted <hi rend="spaced">that</hi> it is so, let him no longer be worthy to stand or <hi rend="spaced">bear witness</hi>, <hi rend="bold">because he has lost his lawfulness</hi>, and therefore let him pay to the king or to the lord of the land <hi rend="bold">X shillings,</hi> which the <hi rend="bold">Danes</hi> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">halsfang</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">aliquem de</hi> seruitoribus altaris occiderit, sit exul contra Deum et contra <hi rend="spaced">omnes</hi> homines, nisi per exilium altius emendet, et parentibus etiam; aut purget se purgatione, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> ƿerelade.
passages.en: If anyone kills <hi rend="spaced">one of the</hi> servants of the altar, let him be an outlaw before God and before <hi rend="spaced">all</hi> men, unless he makes amends more deeply through exile, and to the kinsmen also; or let him clear himself with the purgation <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ƿerelade</hi>.

passages.text: Et infra triginta dies incipiat pęnitentiam et emendationem contra Deum et homines.
passages.en: And within thirty days let him begin penance and amends towards God and men.

passages.text: Si quis ordinatum aut alienum per consilium suum perdere fecerit pecuniam aut uitam, tunc debet esse rex illi pro parente et pro <hi rend="spaced">domino</hi>, nisi alium habeat.
passages.en: If anyone through his counsel causes a man in orders or a stranger to lose money or life, then the king must be to him for kinsman and for <hi rend="spaced">lord</hi>, unless he has another.

passages.text: Et emendetur regi secundum quod iustum est, aut ipse rex districte uindicet <hi rend="spaced">quod factum est</hi>,
passages.en: And let amends be made to the king according to what is right, or let the king himself strictly avenge <hi rend="spaced">what has been done</hi>,

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">quia</hi> Christiano regi conuenit et decet, ut acriter uindicet in <hi rend="spaced">eos qui leges Dei uiolant</hi>.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">because</hi> it befits and becomes a Christian king that he sharply take vengeance on <hi rend="spaced">those who violate the laws of God</hi>.

passages.text: Si minister altaris homicidium fecerit aut aliquod magnum scelus, careat et ordine et <hi rend="spaced">liberalitate</hi> sua et uadat in exilium, secundum quod papa sibi constituerit.
passages.en: If a minister of the altar commits homicide or some great crime, let him lose both his order and his <hi rend="spaced">rank</hi> and go into exile, according to what the pope appoints for him.

passages.text: Quodsi purgare se uoluerit, triplici <hi rend="spaced">sacramento</hi> se purget.
passages.en: But if he wishes to clear himself, let him clear himself with a threefold <hi rend="spaced">oath</hi>.

passages.text: Et nisi infra triginta dies emendationem inceperit et Deo et ho<hi rend="spaced">minibus satisfecerit, expellatur a terra</hi> et sit exul.
passages.en: And unless within thirty days he has begun amends and to both God and <hi rend="spaced">men made satisfaction, let him be driven from the land</hi> and be an outlaw.

passages.text: Si quis aliquem ordinatum ligauerit aut ceciderit aut turpiter deriserit, emendet illi secundum quod iustum est — <hi rend="bold">scilicet secundum modum ordinis</hi> —, et episcopo altaris emendationem, <hi rend="spaced">quod dicitur</hi> þeofodbote, et domino aut regi plenum despectum, <hi rend="spaced">omnia ista</hi> secundum modum ordinis; aut purget se plena purgatione.
passages.en: If anyone binds or beats or shamefully mocks someone in orders, let him make amends to him according to what is right — <hi rend="bold">namely according to the measure of his order</hi> —, and to the bishop the altar-amends, <hi rend="spaced">which is called</hi> <hi rend="italic">þeofodbote</hi>, and to the lord or the king the full contempt-fine, <hi rend="spaced">all these</hi> according to the measure of the order; or let him clear himself with full purgation.

passages.text: Si quis latro <hi rend="spaced">aut alius</hi> condemnatus ad mortem quęrit confessionem, nullo modo ei denegetur.
passages.en: If a thief <hi rend="spaced">or another</hi> condemned to death seeks confession, let it in no way be denied him.

passages.text: Quod si <hi rend="spaced">quis fecerit</hi>, regi emendet; aut purget se sexto.
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">anyone does so</hi>, let him make amends to the king; or clear himself as one of six.

passages.text: Nullus <hi rend="spaced">latro aut</hi> morte condemnatus die Dominico <hi rend="bold">aut</hi><hi rend="bold"> alio</hi><hi rend="bold"> aliquo die</hi><hi rend="bold"> festiuo</hi> occidatur, nisi fugere aut pugnare <hi rend="spaced">uoluerit</hi>; sed custodiatur, quoad usque festiuitas transeat.
passages.en: Let no <hi rend="spaced">thief or</hi> man condemned to death be killed on the Lord's day <hi rend="bold">or on any other feast day</hi>, unless he <hi rend="spaced">wishes</hi> to flee or fight; but let him be guarded until the feast passes.

passages.text: Si liber homo festiuo die operetur et <hi rend="spaced">ita festiuitatem uiolauerit</hi>, <hi rend="bold">decem</hi><hi rend="bold"> solidos</hi> persoluat, et tamen Deo satisfaciat.
passages.en: If a free man works on a feast day and <hi rend="spaced">so violates the feast</hi>, let him pay <hi rend="bold">ten shillings</hi>, and nonetheless make satisfaction to God.

passages.text: Si seruus <hi rend="spaced">hoc faciat</hi>, careat corio suo aut emendet secundum modum operis.
passages.en: If a slave <hi rend="spaced">does this</hi>, let him lose his hide or make amends according to the measure of the deed.

passages.text: Sin autem <hi rend="spaced">inuitus</hi>, domino suo <hi rend="spaced">pręcipiente</hi>, hoc fecerit, dominus careat seruo illo et det <hi rend="bold">halsfang;</hi> seruus autem sit omnino liber; aut dominus purget se.
passages.en: But if he did this <hi rend="spaced">unwilling</hi>, at his lord's <hi rend="spaced">command</hi>, let the lord lose that slave and give <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">halsfang</hi>;</hi> and let the slave be wholly free; or let the lord clear himself.

passages.text: Si liber homo ieiunium uiolauerit, secundum Danos lahslit <seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(id est X solidos)</hi></seg> reddat, secundum Anglos ad qualitatem <hi rend="spaced">ieiunii</hi>.
passages.en: If a free man breaks a fast, according to the Danes let him pay <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(that is, X shillings)</hi></seg>, according to the English by the nature <hi rend="spaced">of the fast</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">seruus</hi> ieiunium uiolauerit carnem manducando, uerberetur secundum modum culpę.
passages.en: If a <hi rend="spaced">slave</hi> breaks a fast by eating meat, let him be beaten according to the measure of the fault.

passages.text: Si quis uiolauerit ieiunium quadragesimale aut pugnando aut rapiendo aut mulierem <hi rend="spaced">ducendo</hi> aut aliquid mali magni faciendo, dupliciter emendet secundum emendationem operis <hi rend="spaced">uiolatę</hi> festiuitatis.
passages.en: If anyone violates the Lenten fast either by fighting or by robbing or by <hi rend="spaced">marrying</hi> a woman or by doing some great evil, let him make double amends according to the amends for the deed of a <hi rend="spaced">violated</hi> feast.

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">si negauerit</hi>, triplici purgatione id neget.
passages.en: And <hi rend="spaced">if he denies it</hi>, let him deny it with a threefold purgation.

passages.text: Si quis aliquam ęcclesiasticarum rectitudinum armis defenderit, <hi rend="bold">decem solidos</hi> secundum Danos emendet; si negauerit, accipiat undecim et ipse sit duodecimus et <hi rend="spaced">ita se purget</hi>.
passages.en: If anyone defends any of the church's rights with arms, let him make amends of <hi rend="bold">ten shillings</hi> according to the Danes; if he denies it, let him take eleven and himself be the twelfth and <hi rend="spaced">so clear himself</hi>.

passages.text: Quodsi ibi <hi rend="spaced">aliquem</hi> uulnerauerit, id <hi rend="spaced">illi</hi> emendet cui <hi rend="spaced">uulnus</hi> fecit, et domino <hi rend="spaced">illius plenam</hi> forisfacturam, et <hi rend="spaced">manum suam</hi> ab episcopo redimat aut perdat.
passages.en: But if he wounds <hi rend="spaced">anyone</hi> there, let him make amends for it <hi rend="spaced">to him</hi> on whom he inflicted the <hi rend="spaced">wound</hi>, and to the lord <hi rend="spaced">of that man the full</hi> forfeiture, and let him redeem <hi rend="spaced">his hand</hi> from the bishop or lose it.

passages.text: Et si hominem occiderit, sit exul et cum clamore expellatur <hi rend="spaced">ab omnibus</hi> <hi rend="spaced">qui Dei iusticiam</hi> uolunt.
passages.en: And if he kills a man, let him be an outlaw and be driven out with hue and cry <hi rend="spaced">by all</hi> <hi rend="spaced">who</hi> want <hi rend="spaced">God's justice</hi>.

passages.text: Et si <hi rend="spaced">ipse</hi> occisus fuerit, <hi rend="spaced">propterea</hi> quia contra iusticiam pugnauerit, iaceat impersolutus, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi>)</seg> ægylde.
passages.en: And if <hi rend="spaced">he himself</hi> is killed, <hi rend="spaced">for the reason</hi> that he fought against justice, let him lie unpaid for, <hi rend="spaced">which the English say</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">call</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">ægylde</hi>.

passages.text: Quicunque uiolauerit ordinem, <hi rend="bold">sicut</hi><hi rend="bold"> est aut</hi><hi rend="bold"> monachum aut presbyterum aut aliquem ordinatum uerberauerit aut aliquid huiusmodi fecerit,</hi> hęc ita emendet secundum modum <hi rend="spaced">ordinis</hi><hi rend="spaced"> patientis</hi>: aut secundum prętium, id est þere, aut secundum forisfacturam aut secundum omnia quę habet <hi rend="spaced">malefactor</hi>.
passages.en: Whoever violates holy orders, <hi rend="bold">as when he beats either a monk or a priest or anyone in orders or does anything of this kind,</hi> let him make amends for these things thus according to the measure of <hi rend="spaced">the order of the injured party</hi>: either according to the price, that is <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>, or according to the forfeiture, or according to all that the <hi rend="spaced">wrongdoer</hi> has.

passages.text: Si coniugium quis uiolauerit, <hi rend="bold">uidelicet iacendo sub coniuge sua,</hi> et fornicatus fuerit cum <hi rend="spaced">alia femina</hi> uel, quod peius est, cum alterius coniugata, faciat pęnitentiam <hi rend="bold">secundum librum pęnitentialem.</hi>
passages.en: If anyone violates marriage, <hi rend="bold">namely while lying under [i.e. bound to] his own wife,</hi> and fornicates with <hi rend="spaced">another woman</hi> or, what is worse, with another man's wife, let him do penance <hi rend="bold">according to the penitential book.</hi>

passages.text: [52] Uidua <hi rend="spaced">etiam</hi>, si ui rapta fuerit, et cum ea coitus factus sit, <hi rend="bold">simili</hi> prętio persoluatur.
passages.en: [52] A widow <hi rend="spaced">also</hi>, if she is carried off by force, and intercourse has been had with her, let it be paid for with a <hi rend="bold">like</hi> price.

passages.text: [52, 1] Si quis uirginem ui rapuerit et cum ea coierit, reddat eam pretio suo, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi> þere.
passages.en: [52, 1] If anyone carries off a virgin by force and lies with her, let him pay for her with her price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi> <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>.

passages.text: [52, 1] Si quis uirginem ui rapuerit et cum ea coierit, reddat eam pretio suo, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi> þere.
passages.en: [52, 1] If anyone carries off a virgin by force and lies with her, let him pay for her with her price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi> <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>.

passages.text: Mulier, quę, uiuente uiro, cum altero uiro adulterata fuerit, et apertum factum sit, fiat sibi ipsi ad opprobrium seculi, et uir eius legalis habeat omnia sua; sed illa careat naso et auribus.
passages.en: A woman who, while her husband is living, commits adultery with another man, and it is made public, let her become for herself a disgrace before the world, and let her lawful husband have all her property; but let her lose nose and ears.

passages.text: Si autem <hi rend="spaced">negauerit</hi> et pur<hi rend="spaced">gare se uoluerit</hi>, et in <hi rend="bold">iudicio</hi> ceciderit, episcopus <hi rend="spaced">uideat</hi> et districte iudicet.
passages.en: But if she <hi rend="spaced">denies</hi> it and <hi rend="spaced">wishes to clear herself</hi>, and fails in the <hi rend="bold">ordeal</hi>, let the bishop <hi rend="spaced">look into it</hi> and judge strictly.

passages.text: Si uir legalem coniugem habens fornicatus cum ancilla sua fuerit, careat ancilla illa et pro semet ipso Deo et hominibus emendet.
passages.en: If a man having a lawful wife fornicates with his slave-woman, let him lose that slave-woman and make amends for himself to God and men.

passages.text: Qui habet legalem coniugem et etiam concubinam, nullus presbiter <hi rend="bold">nec aliquis alius</hi> faciat sibi aliquod seruitium, quod Christiano fieri debet, antequam cessauerit.
passages.en: Whoever has a lawful wife and also a concubine, let no priest <hi rend="bold">nor anyone else</hi> do him any service that ought to be done for a Christian, until he has desisted.

passages.text: Alieni nisi <hi rend="spaced">legale</hi> coniugium <hi rend="spaced">custodierint</hi>, expellantur de terra cum substantia et peccatis.
passages.en: If foreigners do not <hi rend="spaced">keep</hi> <hi rend="spaced">lawful</hi> marriage, let them be expelled from the land with their goods and sins.

passages.text: Si apertum mordrum fuerit, ut aliquis <hi rend="spaced">per illud</hi> occidatur, reddatur parentibus suis.
passages.en: If there is open murder, so that someone is killed <hi rend="spaced">by it</hi>, let him be handed over to his kinsmen.

passages.text: Et si <hi rend="spaced">purgatio</hi> euenerit, et in purgatione ceciderit, episcopus <hi rend="spaced">uideat et iudicet</hi>.
passages.en: And if <hi rend="spaced">a purgation</hi> comes about, and he fails in the purgation, let the bishop <hi rend="spaced">see and judge</hi>.

passages.text: Qui de traditione regis aut domini sui insidiatur, careat omnium bonorum suorum et reus sit mortis, nisi se <hi rend="spaced">purgauerit</hi> triplici iudicio.
passages.en: Whoever plots treachery against the king or his lord, let him lose all his goods and be guilty of death, unless he <hi rend="spaced">clears</hi> himself by a threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Si quis plegium regis fregerit, emendet quinque libris.
passages.en: If anyone breaks the king's pledge, let him make amends with five pounds.

passages.text: Et qui fregerit plegium archiepiscopi aut reguli, <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli uocant</hi> æðeling, III libr. emendet;
passages.en: And whoever breaks the pledge of an archbishop or of a prince, <hi rend="spaced">whom the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">æðeling</hi>, let him make amends with III pounds;

passages.text: episcopi aut comitis II libr. emendet.
passages.en: of a bishop or an earl, let him make amends with II pounds.

passages.text: Si quis pugnam fecerit in <seg type="recension">(regali)</seg> aula regis, careat uita, nisi ei rex parcere uoluerit. . . .
passages.en: If anyone fights in the <seg type="recension">(royal)</seg> hall of the king, let him lose his life, unless the king wishes to spare him. . . .

passages.text: . . . . Qui ante archiepiscopum pugnauerit aut arma extraxerit, <hi rend="bold">quadraginta</hi> solidos emendet; <hi rend="spaced">et</hi> qui hoc ante episcopum uel comitem <hi rend="spaced">fecerit</hi>, <hi rend="bold">uiginti</hi> sol. emendet.
passages.en: . . . . Whoever fights or draws weapons before the archbishop, let him make amends with <hi rend="bold">forty</hi> shillings; <hi rend="spaced">and</hi> whoever <hi rend="spaced">does</hi> this before a bishop or an earl, let him make amends with <hi rend="bold">twenty</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Si quis uaccam aut equam, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant stodmere</hi>, et uitulum uel pullum <hi rend="spaced">cum eis furatus fuerit, pullum soluat</hi> <hi rend="bold">duodecim denariis</hi> <hi rend="spaced">et uitulum similiter</hi> et matres secundum pretium earum.
passages.en: If anyone <hi rend="spaced">steals</hi> a cow or a mare, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call <hi rend="italic">stodmere</hi></hi>, and a calf or a foal <hi rend="spaced">with them, let him pay for the foal</hi> <hi rend="bold">with twelve pence</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and for the calf likewise</hi> and for the mothers according to their price.

passages.text: Si quis commendauerit <hi rend="spaced">aliquem</hi> <hi rend="spaced">hominem alicui homini</hi> <hi rend="bold">non parenti</hi>, et ipse <hi rend="spaced">commendatus perierit in ipsa commendatione</hi>, et aliquis eum calumniauerit, <hi rend="spaced">quod dolositate eius</hi> <hi rend="spaced">perierit</hi>, purget se . . . .
passages.en: If anyone entrusts <hi rend="spaced">some</hi> <hi rend="spaced">man to another man</hi> <hi rend="bold">not a kinsman</hi>, and the <hi rend="spaced">entrusted man himself perishes while in that keeping</hi>, and someone accuses him <hi rend="spaced">that through his treachery</hi> he <hi rend="spaced">perished</hi>, let him clear himself . . . .

passages.incn: II 59d; e; f; g; h; i
passages.text: Si quis ante comitem in placito pugnauerit, emendet secundum pretium <hi rend="bold">sui ipsius</hi> et forisfacturam, <hi rend="spaced">quod</hi> <hi rend="spaced">Angli dicunt</hi> ƿer ⁊ ƿite; et ante hoc <hi rend="spaced">soluat</hi> comiti <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> sol.
passages.en: If anyone fights before the earl at a court meeting, let him make amends according to the price <hi rend="bold">of himself</hi> and the forfeiture, <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ƿer</hi> ⁊ <hi rend="italic">ƿite</hi>; and before this let him <hi rend="spaced">pay</hi> the earl <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> shillings.

passages.incn: II 59d; e; f; g; h; i
passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Et si placitum</hi> populi erexerit, propter extractionem armorum <hi rend="spaced">suorum</hi>, <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> sol. <hi rend="spaced">soluat</hi> comiti.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">And if</hi> he stirs up <hi rend="spaced">the assembly</hi> of the people by drawing <hi rend="spaced">his</hi> weapons, let him <hi rend="spaced">pay</hi> the earl <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> shillings.

passages.incn: II 59d; e; f; g; h; i
passages.text: Si autem tale quid factum fuerit ante <hi rend="bold">uicecomitem</hi> aut ante capellanum regis, XXX sol. <hi rend="spaced">emendet</hi>.
passages.en: But if such a thing is done before the <hi rend="bold">sheriff</hi> or before the king's chaplain, let him <hi rend="spaced">make amends</hi> with XXX shillings.

passages.incn: II 59d; e; f; g; h; i
passages.text: Si quis pugnam <hi rend="spaced">inierit</hi> <hi rend="bold">in aula comitis, XX sol. emendet</hi>, et si <hi rend="bold">hoc fit</hi> in domo hominis <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli uocant</hi> ceorl<hi rend="bold">man</hi> <seg type="recension">(uel <hi rend="bold">ceorlboren</hi>)</seg> VI sol. ei <hi rend="spaced">emendet</hi>.
passages.en: If anyone <hi rend="spaced">starts</hi> a fight <hi rend="bold">in the earl's hall, let him make amends with XX shillings</hi>, and if <hi rend="bold">this happens</hi> in the house of a man <hi rend="spaced">whom the English call</hi> ceorl<hi rend="bold">man</hi> <seg type="recension">(or <hi rend="bold">ceorlboren</hi>)</seg>, let him <hi rend="spaced">make amends</hi> to him with VI shillings.

passages.incn: II 59d; e; f; g; h; i
passages.text: Si arma extraxerit et non pugnauerit, III sol. <hi rend="spaced">emendet</hi>.
passages.en: If he draws weapons and does not fight, let him <hi rend="spaced">make amends</hi> with III shillings.

passages.incn: II 59d; e; f; g; h; i
passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Si autem hoc fit in domo hominis</hi> <hi rend="bold">quem Angli nominant</hi> <hi rend="bold">radcniht,</hi> alii uero sexhende<hi rend="bold">man</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">ter</hi> <hi rend="spaced">carius</hi> <hi rend="spaced">ei emendetur</hi>, <hi rend="bold">id est XVIII sol.</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">quam illi</hi> <hi rend="bold">quem supra nominauimus ceorlman.</hi> Si <hi rend="spaced">in domo</hi> <hi rend="bold">liberalis, quem supra thegen nominauimus</hi> <hi rend="spaced">et quem</hi> <hi rend="spaced">quidam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi> twelfhende<hi rend="bold">man</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">hoc fit</hi>, dupliciter ei <hi rend="spaced">emendetur</hi> plus quam illi <hi rend="spaced">quem</hi> sexhende<hi rend="bold">man</hi> <hi rend="bold">nominauimus, id est XXXVI sol.</hi> . . . .
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">But if this happens in the house of a man</hi> <hi rend="bold">whom the English name</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">radcniht</hi>,</hi> but others <hi rend="italic">sexhende</hi><hi rend="bold">man</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">three times</hi> <hi rend="spaced">more dearly</hi> <hi rend="spaced">let amends be made to him</hi>, <hi rend="bold">that is XVIII shillings</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">than to him</hi> <hi rend="bold">whom we named above <hi rend="italic">ceorlman</hi>.</hi> If <hi rend="spaced">in the house</hi> <hi rend="bold">of a man of rank, whom we named above thegen,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and whom</hi> <hi rend="spaced">some</hi> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> twelfhende<hi rend="bold">man</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">this happens</hi>, doubly <hi rend="spaced">let amends be made</hi> to him, more than to him <hi rend="spaced">whom</hi> <hi rend="bold">we named</hi> <hi rend="italic">sexhende</hi><hi rend="bold">man</hi>, <hi rend="bold">that is XXXVI shillings</hi> . . . .

passages.text: . . . Si quis exarmauerit hominem contra iusticiam, <hi rend="bold">X</hi><hi rend="bold"> sol.</hi> ei emendet; et si ligatus fuerit, medietas pretii eius, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> be healue þere, ei persoluatur.
passages.en: . . . If anyone disarms a man against justice, let him make amends to him with <hi rend="bold">X shillings</hi>; and if he is bound, let half his price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> be healue <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>, be paid to him.

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">in bello</hi> pacem fregerit, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> griþbrece, reus est mortis aut prętii sui.
passages.en: If anyone breaks the peace <hi rend="spaced">in war</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">griþbrece</hi>, he is guilty of death or of his price.

passages.text: Si quis inuasionem domus <hi rend="spaced">aut</hi> curię fecerit, quod <hi rend="spaced">Angli</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> hamsocne <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi>, quinque libras regi emendet.
passages.en: If anyone makes an attack on a house <hi rend="spaced">or</hi> a court, which <hi rend="spaced">the English</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">hamsocne</hi>, let him make amends to the king with five pounds.

passages.text: Et si in illa <hi rend="spaced">inuasione</hi> occisus fuerit, iaceat impersolutus, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> ægelde.
passages.en: And if he is killed in that <hi rend="spaced">attack</hi>, let him lie unpaid for, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ægelde</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis rapinam fecerit, soluat et persoluat, et sit reus pretii sui contra regem.
passages.en: If anyone commits robbery, let him give back and pay compensation, and be liable for his price to the king.

passages.text: Destructio domus et combustio <hi rend="spaced">illius</hi> et <hi rend="spaced">publicus latro</hi> et mordrum et <hi rend="spaced">insidiator</hi> proprii <hi rend="spaced">domini</hi> <seg type="recension">(traditor)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">transeunt</hi> omnem emendationem nec <hi rend="spaced">aliquam</hi> habent.
passages.en: Destruction of a house and burning <hi rend="spaced">of it</hi> and <hi rend="spaced">a public thief</hi> and murder and <hi rend="spaced">a plotter against</hi> his own <hi rend="spaced">lord</hi> <seg type="recension">(traitor)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">go beyond</hi> all amends, nor do they have <hi rend="spaced">any</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis neglexerit emendationem ciuitatis uel pontis aut ire ad <hi rend="spaced">bellum</hi>, soluat regi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> solidos; aut ita sé purget: nominentur ei quattuordecim, et adquirat undecim et <hi rend="spaced">ipse</hi><hi rend="spaced"> sit duodecimus</hi>.
passages.en: If anyone neglects the repair of a town or a bridge or going to <hi rend="spaced">war</hi>, let him pay the king <hi rend="bold">XL</hi> shillings; or let him clear himself thus: let fourteen be named for him, and let him obtain eleven and <hi rend="spaced">himself be the twelfth</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis Godes flyman iniuste habuerit, reddat eum ad iusticiam et persoluat <hi rend="bold">despectum</hi> cui iustum est; et regi emendet pretium, id <hi rend="spaced">est be</hi> þere.
passages.en: If anyone unjustly harbours <hi rend="italic">Godes flyman</hi> [God's fugitive], let him deliver him to justice and pay the <hi rend="bold">contempt-fine</hi> to whom it is due; and to the king let him pay amends of his price, that <hi rend="spaced">is be</hi> <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis secum tenuerit excommunicatum aut exulem <hi rend="spaced">clamatum, careat omnibus</hi> bonis suis et uita, <hi rend="bold">nisi ei</hi><hi rend="bold"> rex parcat.</hi>
passages.en: If anyone keeps with him an excommunicate or a <hi rend="spaced">proclaimed</hi> outlaw, <hi rend="spaced">let him lose all</hi> his goods and his life, <hi rend="bold">unless the king spares him.</hi>

passages.text: Hęc est alleuiatio, quam ego uolo fieri omni populo, unde hactenus ultra modum fuerunt grauati.
passages.en: This is the relief which I wish to be made for all the people, in which hitherto they have been burdened beyond measure.

passages.text: Hoc est inprimis: pręcipio omnibus prępositis meis, ut in propriis <hi rend="bold">uillis</hi> meis bene et <hi rend="spaced">pleniter</hi> arent et <hi rend="bold">seminent et culturas optime colant</hi> et inde me et <hi rend="spaced">meos</hi> pascant, et a nullo aliquid <hi rend="bold">iniuste extorqueant,</hi> unde me pascere possint <seg type="recension">(debeant)</seg>, nisi quis sponte et <hi rend="spaced">uoluntarie</hi> eis aliquod auxilium prębere uoluerit.
passages.en: This is first: I command all my reeves that on my own <hi rend="bold">estates</hi> they plough well and <hi rend="spaced">fully</hi> and <hi rend="bold">sow and cultivate the fields excellently</hi> and from that feed me and <hi rend="spaced">mine</hi>, and from no one <hi rend="bold">unjustly extort</hi> anything with which they could <seg type="recension">(should)</seg> feed me, unless someone of his own accord and <hi rend="spaced">willingly</hi> wishes to offer them some help.

passages.text: Quodsi aliquis dehinc forisfacturam aliquam exegerit ab aliquo, <hi rend="bold">qui eos adiuuare ad hoc noluerit,</hi> pretium suum, <hi rend="spaced">id est</hi> þere, regi <hi rend="spaced">persoluat</hi>.
passages.en: But if anyone henceforth exacts any forfeiture from someone <hi rend="bold">who would not help them in this,</hi> let him <hi rend="spaced">pay</hi> his price, <hi rend="spaced">that is</hi> <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>, to the king.

passages.text: Si quis obmutescit, <hi rend="spaced">antequam</hi> ex hac uita exeat, seu per neglegentiam seu per subitam mortem, dominus eius nichil se intromittat de omnibus bonis illius, nisi quantum ad eum iuste <hi rend="spaced">pertinet</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">hoc est tantum quod Angli uocant</hi> heregeate.
passages.en: If anyone falls dumb <hi rend="spaced">before</hi> he goes out of this life, whether through negligence or through sudden death, let his lord not meddle at all with any of his goods, except as much as rightly <hi rend="spaced">belongs</hi> to him, <hi rend="spaced">that is, just what the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">heregeate</hi>.

passages.text: Sed omnia illius <hi rend="spaced">diuidantur</hi> secundum ordinationem suam mulieri et infantibus et parentibus <hi rend="spaced">suis</hi>.
passages.en: But let all his things <hi rend="spaced">be divided</hi> according to his disposition among wife and children and <hi rend="spaced">his</hi> kinsmen.

passages.text: Et illud debitum, quod heregeat supra <hi rend="spaced">nominauimus</hi>, ita conuenienter pręparetur, secundum quod <hi rend="bold">natus est:</hi>
passages.en: And that due, which above we <hi rend="spaced">named</hi> <hi rend="italic">heregeat</hi>, let it be suitably prepared thus, according to what <hi rend="bold">he was born [to]:</hi>

passages.text: Comitis, sicut <hi rend="spaced">decet</hi><hi rend="spaced"> comiti</hi>, id est octo equos, IIII cum sellis et quattuor sine sellis, IIII galeas et quattuor loricas, octo lanceas et totidem scuta et <hi rend="bold">quinquaginta</hi> mancas auri.
passages.en: Of an earl, as <hi rend="spaced">befits an earl</hi>, that is eight horses, IIII with saddles and four without saddles, IIII helmets and four mail-coats, eight lances and as many shields and <hi rend="bold">fifty</hi> mancuses of gold.

passages.text: Mediocris hominis, <hi rend="bold">quem</hi><hi rend="bold"> Angli dicunt læsseþegen</hi><hi rend="bold">,</hi> illius <hi rend="spaced">heregeat</hi> est: equus et arma aut halsfang, <hi rend="spaced">quod est</hi> <hi rend="bold">X</hi><hi rend="bold"> solidi,</hi> in þeassexe; in Mercia <hi rend="spaced">uero</hi> et in Eastengle duę librę <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">denariorum</hi>)</seg>.
passages.en: Of a middling man, <hi rend="bold">whom the English call <hi rend="italic">læsseþegen</hi>,</hi> his <hi rend="spaced"><hi rend="italic">heregeat</hi></hi> is: a horse and arms or <hi rend="italic">halsfang</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which is</hi> <hi rend="bold">X shillings,</hi> in þeassexe [Wessex]; in Mercia <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> and in Eastengle [East Anglia] two pounds <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">of pence</hi>)</seg>.

passages.text: Liberalis hominis qui habet consuetudines suas, <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli dicunt</hi> kinges þegen, debitum <hi rend="spaced">post mortem eius</hi>, quod supra <hi rend="spaced">nominauimus</hi> heregeat: IIII librę;
passages.en: Of a free man of rank (thegn) who has his customs, <hi rend="spaced">whom the English call</hi> kinges <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi>, the due <hi rend="spaced">after his death</hi>, which above we <hi rend="spaced">named</hi> <hi rend="italic">heregeat</hi>: IIII pounds;

passages.text: et, si notus fuerit regi: duos equos, unus cum sella et alius sine, gladium unum et duas lanceas et duo scuta et quinquaginta mancas auri;
passages.en: and, if he was known to the king: two horses, one with a saddle and the other without, one sword and two lances and two shields and fifty mancuses of gold;

passages.text: et qui tantum non <seg type="recension">(habet uel)</seg> potest, XL <hi rend="spaced">solidos</hi>.
passages.en: and he who cannot <seg type="recension">(has not or)</seg> [pay] so much: XL <hi rend="spaced">shillings</hi>.

passages.text: Ubi <hi rend="spaced">homo</hi> sine aliqua calumpnia, aut de <hi rend="spaced">terra</hi> <hi rend="bold">aut de alia re,</hi> moritur, uxor eius et pueri remaneant <hi rend="spaced">similiter</hi>.
passages.en: Where a <hi rend="spaced">man</hi> dies without any claim [against him], either concerning <hi rend="spaced">land</hi> <hi rend="bold">or concerning another thing,</hi> his wife and children shall remain <hi rend="spaced">likewise</hi> [undisturbed].

passages.text: Si autem uir ante mortem proclamatus <hi rend="spaced">de talibus fuit</hi>, oportet ut <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">eius</hi>)</seg> heredes secundum <hi rend="spaced">iusticiam</hi> respondeant, sicut ipse deberet, si uiueret.
passages.en: But if the man before his death was <hi rend="spaced">accused of such things</hi>, it is necessary that <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">his</hi>)</seg> heirs answer according to <hi rend="spaced">justice</hi>, as he himself would have had to, if he were alive.

passages.text: Et uidua per integrum annum sine uiro permaneat.
passages.en: And the widow shall remain without a husband for an entire year.

passages.text: Quę si ante annum aliter fecerit <seg type="recension">(nupserit)</seg>, careat dote et omnibus bonis, quę habuit per primum uirum; et proximi paren<hi rend="spaced">tes prioris uiri</hi> habeant terras et <hi rend="spaced">alia omnia</hi>, quę illa <hi rend="spaced">iuste perdidit</hi>.
passages.en: If she before the year does otherwise <seg type="recension">(marries)</seg>, she shall lose her dower and all the goods which she had through her first husband; and the nearest <hi rend="spaced">kinsmen of the former husband</hi> shall have the lands and <hi rend="spaced">all other things</hi> which she <hi rend="spaced">has justly lost</hi>.

passages.text: Uir autem post acceptus sit reus prętii sui contra regem aut contra eum, cui hoc rex concesserit.
passages.en: But the man afterwards accepted shall be liable for his own price [wergeld] to the king or to him to whom the king has granted this.

passages.text: Et quamuis coacta fuisset il<hi rend="spaced">lum accipere</hi>, nisi ab illo omnino recedat, ita ut eius nunquam amplius fiat, careat om<hi rend="spaced">nium supra</hi><hi rend="spaced"> dictorum</hi> bonorum.
passages.en: And although she had been forced to <hi rend="spaced">accept him</hi>, unless she withdraws from him entirely, so that she never again becomes his, she shall lose <hi rend="spaced">all the above-mentioned</hi> goods.

passages.text: Et tamen <hi rend="spaced">interdicimus</hi>, ne uidua ultra modum cito ueletur.
passages.en: And yet we <hi rend="spaced">forbid</hi> that a widow be veiled too hastily.

passages.text: Sed persoluat redditum do<hi rend="spaced">mino suo, quod supra</hi> heregeat <hi rend="spaced">nominauimus</hi>, infra duodecim menses, nisi ei ante oportunum fuerit.
passages.en: But she shall pay the due to her <hi rend="spaced">lord, which above</hi> we <hi rend="spaced">have named</hi> <hi rend="italic">heregeat</hi> [heriot], within twelve months, unless it is convenient for her earlier.

passages.text: Nemo cogat mulierem aut uir<hi rend="spaced">ginem contra uoluntatem illarum</hi>, quod eis displiceat, nec pro pecunia <hi rend="spaced">nec pro alia re</hi>, nisi quis sponte quid dare uoluerit.
passages.en: Let no one force a woman or a <hi rend="spaced">maiden against their will</hi> to what displeases them, neither for money <hi rend="spaced">nor for any other thing</hi>, unless someone of his own accord wishes to give something.

passages.text: Si quis lanceam suam ad hostium alicuius posuerit et intrauerit domum <hi rend="spaced">aliqua de causa</hi>, aut si alicubi <hi rend="spaced">inuenerit</hi> arma iacere in aliquo <hi rend="spaced">secreto</hi> loco, ubi sine offensione esse possent, si dimitterentur, et ille posuerit ibi lanceam suam, et alius eam inde rapiat et aliquid mali cum illa faciat, tunc rectum est, ut ipse qui <hi rend="spaced">cum lancea malum fecerit</hi>, ipse malum emendet.
passages.en: If anyone has set his lance at someone's door and has entered the house <hi rend="spaced">for some reason</hi>, or if somewhere he <hi rend="spaced">has found</hi> weapons lying in some <hi rend="spaced">secluded</hi> place, where they could be without harm if they were left alone, and he has put his lance there, and another seizes it from there and does some harm with it, then it is right that he himself who <hi rend="spaced">did harm with the lance</hi>, he himself make amends for the harm.

passages.text: Et ille qui <hi rend="spaced">lanceam posuit</hi>, ubi sine <hi rend="spaced">lesione</hi> iacere po<hi rend="spaced">tuisset, si dimitteretur</hi>, purget se, si audet, quod non fuit eius uoluntate nec potestate nec consilio nec testimonio eius <hi rend="spaced">malum factum quod actum</hi> est: erit tunc rectum secundum <hi rend="spaced">iusticiam</hi>, ut ipse sit inculpabilis.
passages.en: And he who <hi rend="spaced">put the lance</hi> where it <hi rend="spaced">could have</hi> lain without <hi rend="spaced">injury</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">if it were left alone</hi>, shall clear himself, if he dares, that it was not by his will nor power nor counsel nor his witness that <hi rend="spaced">the harm which was done was done</hi>: it will then be right according to <hi rend="spaced">justice</hi> that he be blameless.

passages.text: Et malefactor <hi rend="spaced">malum</hi> quod fecit emendet, secundum quod lex docet.
passages.en: And the wrongdoer shall make amends for the <hi rend="spaced">harm</hi> which he did, according as the law teaches.

passages.text: Si quis aliquid <hi rend="spaced">furtiuum</hi> ad domum suam portet, et patefac<hi rend="spaced">tum fuerit</hi>, iustum est, ut habeat quod quesiuit.
passages.en: If anyone carries something <hi rend="spaced">stolen</hi> to his house, and it <hi rend="spaced">has been</hi> discovered, it is just that he have what he sought.

passages.text: Et nisi illud <hi rend="spaced">furtum inuentum</hi> fuerit sub clauibus mulieris, sit illa immunis.
passages.en: And unless the <hi rend="spaced">stolen thing is found</hi> under the woman's keys, she shall be free [of guilt].

passages.text: Has uero <hi rend="spaced">claues mulier</hi> debet sub cura sua custodire, scilicet dispensę suę et arcę et scrinii sui; sub his <hi rend="spaced">itaque clauibus</hi> si <hi rend="spaced">inuentum</hi><hi rend="spaced"> non fuerit</hi>, mulier sine culpa erit.
passages.en: These <hi rend="spaced">keys</hi>, however, <hi rend="spaced">the woman</hi> must keep under her care, namely of her storeroom and her chest and her casket; under these <hi rend="spaced">keys, therefore,</hi> if it <hi rend="spaced">has not been found</hi>, the woman will be without blame.

passages.text: Hactenus <hi rend="spaced">habita</hi> est <hi rend="spaced">quędam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">praua</hi> consuetudo in <hi rend="spaced">hac</hi> terra, quia pueri qui iacebant in cunis, quanuis adhuc nullo cibo uterentur, iudicabantur ab auaris ęque rei, ac si scientiam haberent.
passages.en: Until now there <hi rend="spaced">has been</hi> <hi rend="spaced">a certain</hi> <hi rend="spaced">wicked</hi> custom in <hi rend="spaced">this</hi> land, that children who lay in cradles, although they did not yet take any food, were judged by the greedy equally guilty, as if they had understanding.

passages.text: Sed ego hoc omnibus modis <hi rend="spaced">interdico</hi> et multa alia, quę ualde sunt Deo contraria.
passages.en: But I <hi rend="spaced">forbid</hi> this in every way, and many other things which are very contrary to God.

passages.text: Si quis timore <hi rend="spaced">perterritus</hi> a domino suo aut a <hi rend="spaced">sociis suis</hi> fugerit de bello siue in terra sive in mari <seg type="recension">(aqua)</seg>, careat omnium bonorum suorum cum uita; et dominus <seg type="recension">(suus)</seg> accipiat omnia que illius sunt et terram, si quam ei antea dedisset.
passages.en: If anyone, <hi rend="spaced">terrified</hi> by fear, flees from his lord or from <hi rend="spaced">his comrades</hi> out of battle, whether on land or on sea <seg type="recension">(water)</seg>, he shall lose all his goods along with his life; and the <seg type="recension">(his)</seg> lord shall take all things that are his, and the land, if he had given him any before.

passages.text: Si autem habuerit <hi rend="spaced">alodium</hi>, sit regis.
passages.en: But if he has <hi rend="spaced">allodial land</hi>, it shall be the king's.

passages.text: Si quis uero ceciderit ante dominum suum in bello siue in patria siue extra patriam, <hi rend="spaced">redditus domini sui</hi>, scilicet <seg type="recension">(quem <hi rend="spaced">supra nominauimus</hi>)</seg> heregeat, perdonetur <hi rend="bold">uxori eius uel heredibus</hi><hi rend="bold">;</hi> heredes autem habeant omnia eius cum terris et iuste diuidant.
passages.en: But if anyone falls before his lord in battle, whether in the country or outside the country, <hi rend="spaced">his lord's due</hi>, namely <seg type="recension">(which we <hi rend="spaced">named above</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">heregeat</hi> [heriot], shall be remitted <hi rend="bold">to his wife or heirs;</hi> and the heirs shall have all his things with the lands and divide them justly.

passages.text: Quisquis terram suam iuste defenderit teste comitatu, possideat sine calumnia, dum uiuit, et si placuerit sibi eam uendere aut dare, det cuicunque ei libuerit.
passages.en: Whoever has justly defended his land with the shire (court) as witness shall possess it without claim while he lives, and if it pleases him to sell or give it, let him give it to whomever he pleases.

passages.text: Uolo etiam, ut omnis homo habeat uenationem suam in siluis et in planis super sua.
passages.en: I will also that every man have his hunting in the woods and in the open country on his own [land].

passages.text: Et omnes deuitent meam, ubicunque illam habere uoluero.
passages.en: And let all avoid mine, wherever I wish to have it.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Pręcipimus</hi> etiam, ut omnis homo habeat pacem et securitatem <hi rend="spaced">eundo</hi> et redeundo ad placitum, nisi sit latro publicus <hi rend="spaced">omnino</hi>.
passages.en: We <hi rend="spaced">command</hi> also that every man have peace and security <hi rend="spaced">going</hi> and returning to the court, unless he is <hi rend="spaced">altogether</hi> a public thief.

passages.text: Quisquis has leges, quas rex <hi rend="spaced">modo omnibus hominibus</hi> concessit <hi rend="spaced">et statuit</hi>, sit Anglus sit Danus, uiolauerit, persoluat regi pretium sui ipsius.
passages.en: Whoever, be he English or Dane, violates these laws which the king has <hi rend="spaced">now granted to all men</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and established</hi>, shall pay to the king his own price.

passages.text: Si secundo <hi rend="spaced">hoc idem fecerit</hi>, dupliciter <hi rend="spaced">secundum superiorem rationem</hi> emendet.
passages.en: If a second time he <hi rend="spaced">does this same thing</hi>, he shall make amends doubly <hi rend="spaced">according to the above reckoning</hi>.

passages.text: Quod si <hi rend="spaced">audendo</hi> tertio hoc presumpserit, perdat omnia sua. . . . . . .
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">daringly</hi> a third time he presumes this, he shall lose all his things. . . . . . .

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Si quis aliquid</hi><hi rend="small">, <hi rend="spaced">pro aliqua forisfactura</hi>, accipiat</hi><hi rend="small">, antequam iuste</hi><hi rend="small"> rectitudinem petat, reddat quod accepit et</hi><hi rend="small"> secundo persoluat; et</hi> <seg type="recension">(regi)</seg> <hi rend="small">quadraginta</hi><hi rend="small"> solidos reddat</hi> <seg type="recension">(aut illi)</seg> qui habet sacam et socnam suam; et insuper prętium suum domino suo.
passages.en: <hi rend="small">If anyone takes something <hi rend="spaced">for some forfeiture</hi> before he justly seeks right, he shall give back what he took and pay a second time; and</hi> <seg type="recension">(to the king)</seg> <hi rend="small">shall pay forty shillings</hi> <seg type="recension">(or to him)</seg> who has his sake and soke; and in addition his price to his lord.

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Latrones appellamus usque VII homines, a septem usque XXXV</hi><hi rend="small"> <hi rend="spaced">uocant Angli</hi> hloth</hi><hi rend="small">, a</hi><hi rend="small"> XXXV dehinc</hi><hi rend="small"> erit</hi><hi rend="small"> exercitus.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">We call [them] thieves up to VII men; from seven to XXXV <hi rend="spaced">the English call [it]</hi> <hi rend="italic">hloth</hi> [band], from XXXV onward it will be an army.</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Qui calumniatur</hi><hi rend="small"> de hloth</hi><hi rend="small">, sí negauerit, ita sé purget:</hi> acceptis undecim hominibus, et ipse sit duodecimus; aut despectum calumniantis persoluat et duas libras pro forisfactura ei det qui habet consuetudines suas.
passages.en: <hi rend="small">Whoever is accused of <hi rend="italic">hloth</hi> [band], if he denies it, shall clear himself thus:</hi> having taken eleven men, he himself being the twelfth; or he shall pay the accuser's contempt [fine] and give two pounds as forfeiture to him who has his customs.

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Et si quis calumniatur, quasi</hi><hi rend="small"> ducat exercitum</hi><hi rend="small"> super aliquem, et negauerit, purget se secundum prętium</hi> calumniantis aut eum persoluat.
passages.en: <hi rend="small">And if anyone is accused as though he led an army against someone, and he denies it, he shall clear himself according to the price</hi> of the accuser, or pay it.

passages.text: Si quis per hloth occiderit hominem, <hi rend="bold">quem</hi> <hi rend="bold">quidam</hi> <hi rend="bold">Angli dicunt</hi> tƿihende <hi rend="bold">et alii ceorlman,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">qui illum se occidisse</hi> cognouerit, persoluat <hi rend="spaced">secundum</hi> were <hi rend="spaced">suum et etiam reddat forisfacturas</hi>, et quisque de <hi rend="spaced">sociis eius, qui tunc cum eo</hi> fuerunt, triginta sol. persoluat.
passages.en: If anyone through a <hi rend="italic">hloth</hi> [band] kills a man <hi rend="bold">whom</hi> <hi rend="bold">some</hi> <hi rend="bold">English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">tƿihende</hi> <hi rend="bold">and others <hi rend="italic">ceorlman</hi>,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">he who acknowledges that he killed him</hi> shall pay <hi rend="spaced">according to his</hi> <hi rend="italic">were</hi> [wergeld] <hi rend="spaced">and also render the forfeitures</hi>, and each of <hi rend="spaced">his companions who were then with him</hi> shall pay thirty shillings.

passages.text: Si autem <hi rend="spaced">talis occiditur</hi>, <hi rend="bold">qualem supra</hi> <hi rend="bold">nominauimus radcniht</hi> <hi rend="bold">et quidam</hi> <hi rend="bold">Angli</hi> <hi rend="bold">uocant</hi> sexhendeman, occisor <hi rend="spaced">soluat</hi> ƿer et wite et quisquis <hi rend="spaced">sociorum eius</hi> LX solidos.
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">such a man is killed</hi> <hi rend="bold">as above</hi> <hi rend="bold">we have named <hi rend="italic">radcniht</hi></hi> <hi rend="bold">and some</hi> <hi rend="bold">English</hi> <hi rend="bold">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">sexhendeman</hi>, the slayer shall <hi rend="spaced">pay</hi> <hi rend="italic">ƿer</hi> [wergeld] and <hi rend="italic">wite</hi> [fine] and each <hi rend="spaced">of his companions</hi> LX shillings.

passages.text: Si is, <hi rend="spaced">qui occisus</hi> est, fuit <hi rend="bold">liberalis</hi><hi rend="bold">, id est þegen</hi> <hi rend="bold">sicut</hi> <hi rend="bold">superius diximus:</hi> qui occidit ƿer et ƿite, <hi rend="spaced">singuli autem sociorum eius</hi> CXX solidos.
passages.en: If he <hi rend="spaced">who was killed</hi> was <hi rend="bold">a free man of rank (thegn), that is <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi>,</hi> <hi rend="bold">as</hi> <hi rend="bold">we said above:</hi> he who killed [shall pay] <hi rend="italic">ƿer</hi> [wergeld] and <hi rend="italic">ƿite</hi> [fine], <hi rend="spaced">but each of his companions</hi> CXX shillings.

passages.text: Si illa societas <hi rend="spaced">quam uocauimus</hi> hloth <hi rend="spaced">hęc homicidia</hi> fecerit et postea iuramento hoc negare uoluerit, <hi rend="spaced">tunc omnes simul calumniati</hi> persoluant pretium occisi, <hi rend="spaced">et omnes simul</hi> unam forisfacturam, sicut conueniat pretio, <hi rend="bold">quod Angli dicunt be ƿeres mæðe</hi> . . . .
passages.en: If that association <hi rend="spaced">which we have called</hi> <hi rend="italic">hloth</hi> [band] has committed <hi rend="spaced">these homicides</hi> and afterwards wishes to deny this by oath, <hi rend="spaced">then all those accused together</hi> shall pay the price of the slain man, <hi rend="spaced">and all together</hi> one forfeiture, as befits the price, <hi rend="bold">which the English call <hi rend="italic">be ƿeres mæðe</hi> [according to the measure of the wer]</hi> . . . .

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Emendatio uulnerati capitis est</hi>: si ossa <hi rend="bold">sine</hi> <hi rend="spaced">foramine</hi> sunt, XXX sol.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">The compensation for a wounded head is</hi>: if the bones are <hi rend="bold">without</hi> <hi rend="spaced">perforation</hi>, XXX shillings.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Et si exterior</hi> <hi rend="spaced">os sit perforatum</hi>, XV sol.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">And if the outer</hi> <hi rend="spaced">bone is perforated</hi>, XV shillings.

passages.text: Si infra capillos uulnus fuerit <hi rend="spaced">unius uncię</hi> longum, unum sol. <seg type="recension">(emen)</seg>det.
passages.en: If within the hair there is a wound <hi rend="spaced">of one inch</hi> long, he shall give <seg type="recension">(compensate)</seg> one shilling.

passages.text: Si extra capillos fuerit <hi rend="spaced">et eiusdem magnitudinis, duo</hi> solidi <hi rend="spaced">sint</hi> emendatio.
passages.en: If it is outside the hair <hi rend="spaced">and of the same size, two</hi> shillings <hi rend="spaced">shall be</hi> the compensation.

passages.text: Si cui auris <hi rend="spaced">absciditur</hi>, XXX sol. emend'.
passages.en: If someone's ear <hi rend="spaced">is cut off</hi>, he shall compensate XXX shillings.

passages.text: Si auditus <hi rend="spaced">obturatur, ita ut non possit audire</hi>, LX sol. emend'.
passages.en: If the hearing <hi rend="spaced">is stopped up, so that he cannot hear</hi>, he shall compensate LX shillings.

passages.text: Si cui oculus abscidatur, <hi rend="spaced">talis erit emendatio</hi>: sexaginta sex solidi et sex denarii et tertia pars denarii.
passages.en: If someone's eye is cut out, <hi rend="spaced">the compensation will be such</hi>: sixty-six shillings and six pence and a third part of a penny.

passages.text: Et si oculus <hi rend="spaced">infra caput remanserit</hi>, et tamen nichil cum illo oculo uidere possit, tertia pars <hi rend="bold">stet</hi> <hi rend="bold">in</hi> <hi rend="spaced">emendatione</hi>.
passages.en: And if the eye <hi rend="spaced">remains within the head</hi> and yet he can see nothing with that eye, a third part <hi rend="bold">shall stand</hi> <hi rend="bold">in</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the compensation</hi>.

passages.text: Si cui <hi rend="bold">maxilla</hi> abscidatur, LX sol. emend'.
passages.en: If someone's <hi rend="bold">jaw</hi> is cut off, he shall compensate LX shillings.

passages.text: Si cui dens anterior <seg type="recension">(id est pręcisor)</seg> auellatur, octo sol. emend'.
passages.en: If someone's front tooth <seg type="recension">(that is, incisor)</seg> is pulled out, he shall compensate eight shillings.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">autem</hi> dens <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">caninus</hi>)</seg>, <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli uocant</hi> wengthoþ, sit ablatus, quatuor sol. emend'.
passages.en: If <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> a tooth <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">canine</hi>)</seg>, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">wengthoþ</hi> [cheek-tooth], is knocked out, he shall compensate four shillings.

passages.text: <hi rend="bold">Mandibula,</hi> id est tuxl <seg type="recension">(uel <hi rend="bold">molares</hi>)</seg> hominis, <hi rend="spaced">soluitur quindecim sol.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="bold">The jaw-tooth,</hi> that is <hi rend="italic">tuxl</hi> [tusk] <seg type="recension">(or <hi rend="bold">molars</hi>)</seg> of a man, <hi rend="spaced">is paid for with fifteen shillings.</hi>

passages.text: Si cui os maxillare <hi rend="spaced">confringitur</hi>, quindecim sol. emend'.
passages.en: If someone's jaw-bone <hi rend="spaced">is broken</hi>, he shall compensate fifteen shillings.

passages.text: Mentum <seg type="recension">(id est cinban)</seg> si fissum fuerit, emend' duodecim sol.
passages.en: The chin <seg type="recension">(that is <hi rend="italic">cinban</hi> [chin-bone])</seg>, if it is split, he shall compensate twelve shillings.

passages.text: Si cui gurgulium id est þrotbolle, <hi rend="spaced">perforatum</hi> fuerit, emend' duodecim sol.
passages.en: If someone's gullet, that is <hi rend="italic">þrotbolle</hi> [throat-boll], <hi rend="spaced">is pierced</hi>, he shall compensate twelve shillings.

passages.text: Si cui lingua <hi rend="spaced">abscidatur</hi>, emendatio eius sicut oculi.
passages.en: If someone's tongue <hi rend="spaced">is cut out</hi>, its compensation [is] as [that] of an eye.

passages.text: Si quis uulneratus fuerit in scapulis, ita ut ius <seg type="recension">(id est <hi rend="bold">mæri</hi>)</seg> exeat, triginta sol. emendet.
passages.en: If anyone is wounded in the shoulders so that the fluid <seg type="recension">(that is <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">mæri</hi></hi>)</seg> comes out, he shall compensate thirty shillings.

passages.text: Si quis lacertum alicui fregerit, quindecim sol. emendet.
passages.en: If anyone breaks someone's upper arm, he shall compensate fifteen shillings.

passages.text: Si quis fregerit alicui <hi rend="spaced">utraque</hi> <hi rend="spaced">brachia</hi>, triginta sol. emend.
passages.en: If anyone breaks <hi rend="spaced">both</hi> <hi rend="spaced">arms</hi> of someone, he shall compensate thirty shillings.

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">qui</hi> pollicem <hi rend="spaced">absciderit</hi>, triginta sol. emend.
passages.en: And <hi rend="spaced">he who</hi> <hi rend="spaced">cuts off</hi> a thumb shall compensate thirty shillings.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">quis</hi> ungulam pollicis <hi rend="spaced">absciderit</hi>, quinque sol. emend.
passages.en: If <hi rend="spaced">anyone</hi> <hi rend="spaced">cuts off</hi> the nail of the thumb, he shall compensate five shillings.

passages.text: Secundus digitus <hi rend="spaced">nominatur</hi> index <hi rend="spaced">siue</hi> demonstratorius; <hi rend="spaced">pretium eius est</hi> quindecim sol.; ungule eius <hi rend="bold">V</hi> sol.
passages.en: The second finger <hi rend="spaced">is called</hi> index <hi rend="spaced">or</hi> pointer; <hi rend="spaced">its price is</hi> fifteen shillings; its nail <hi rend="bold">V</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Tertius digitus <hi rend="spaced">qui nominatur impudicus: eius pretium est</hi> duodecim sol. et ungulę eius duo sol.
passages.en: The third finger, <hi rend="spaced">which is called the unchaste: its price is</hi> twelve shillings, and its nail two shillings.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Quartus anularis; pretium</hi> <hi rend="spaced">eius</hi> XVII sol. et ungulę eius quatuor sol.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">The fourth, the ring finger; the price</hi> <hi rend="spaced">of it</hi> XVII shillings, and its nail four shillings.

passages.text: Quintus auricularis; eius pretium nouem sol. et ungule eius unius sol. <hi rend="bold"><seg type="recension">(XII den.)</seg></hi>.
passages.en: The fifth, the ear finger; its price nine shillings, and its nail one shilling <hi rend="bold"><seg type="recension">(XII pence)</seg></hi>.

passages.text: Si quis uulneratur in ilio <seg type="recension">(id est grin)</seg>, triginta solidis emendetur.
passages.en: If anyone is wounded in the groin <seg type="recension">(that is <hi rend="italic">grin</hi>)</seg>, it shall be compensated with thirty shillings.

passages.text: Quodsi ultra fuerit perforatum, <hi rend="spaced">ad utrumque foramen</hi> XX sol., <hi rend="spaced">id est pro uno foramine</hi> XX <hi rend="spaced">sol. et pro alio similiter</hi>.
passages.en: But if it has been pierced right through, <hi rend="spaced">for each hole</hi> XX shillings, <hi rend="spaced">that is, for one hole</hi> XX <hi rend="spaced">shillings and for the other likewise</hi>.

passages.text: Si femur hominis perforatum fuerit, triginta sol. emend.;
passages.en: If a man's thigh is pierced, he shall compensate thirty shillings;

passages.text: et si fractum fuerit, similiter.
passages.en: and if it is broken, likewise.

passages.text: Si tibia perforata fuerit sub genu, duodecim sol. emend.
passages.en: If the shin is pierced below the knee, he shall compensate twelve shillings.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="bold">super</hi> genu fuerit, triginta sol.
passages.en: But if it is <hi rend="bold">above</hi> the knee, thirty shillings.

passages.text: Primus digitus pedis <hi rend="spaced">appretiatur</hi> uiginti sol.,
passages.en: The first toe <hi rend="spaced">is valued at</hi> twenty shillings,

passages.text: secundus quindecim sol.,
passages.en: the second fifteen shillings,

passages.text: medius nouem sol.,
passages.en: the middle one nine shillings,

passages.text: quartus VI sol.,
passages.en: the fourth VI shillings,

passages.text: quintus V sol.
passages.en: the fifth V shillings.

passages.text: Si quis in uerendis ita uulneratur, ut non possit generare infantem, <hi rend="spaced">eius pretium</hi> octoginta sol. emend'.
passages.en: If anyone is so wounded in the genitals that he cannot beget a child, he shall compensate <hi rend="spaced">his price</hi> with eighty shillings.

passages.text: Si cui <hi rend="spaced">abscidatur</hi> brachium cum manu ante cubitum, LXXX sol. emend'.
passages.en: If someone's arm <hi rend="spaced">is cut off</hi> with the hand, before the elbow, he shall compensate LXXX shillings.

passages.text: Omne uulnus <hi rend="spaced">factum</hi> extra capillos et ante manicas <hi rend="bold">et ante cubitum</hi> et <hi rend="spaced">ante genu habebit duplex pretium</hi>.
passages.en: Every wound <hi rend="spaced">made</hi> outside the hair and before the sleeves <hi rend="bold">and before the elbow</hi> and <hi rend="spaced">before the knee shall have a double price</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">assatura renum, quam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi> lendebræde, omnino incisa fuerit, sexaginta sol. emend'.
passages.en: If the <hi rend="spaced">roast of the kidneys, which</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">lendebræde</hi> [loin-roast], is entirely cut through, he shall compensate sixty shillings.

passages.text: Si autem infixa fuerit, quindecim sol. emend'.
passages.en: But if it is stabbed into, he shall compensate fifteen shillings.

passages.text: Si perforata fuerit, XXX sol. emend'.
passages.en: If it is pierced through, he shall compensate XXX shillings.

passages.text: Si quis uulneratur in humero, <hi rend="spaced">si uiuere potest, emendetur</hi> ei octoginta sol.
passages.en: If anyone is wounded in the shoulder, <hi rend="spaced">if he can live, let compensation be made</hi> to him with eighty shillings.

passages.text: Si quis percusserit manum <hi rend="spaced">alterius de foris, si potest mederi, dentur ei</hi> uiginti solidi.
passages.en: If anyone strikes the hand <hi rend="spaced">of another from outside, if it can be healed, let there be given to him</hi> twenty shillings.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">autem</hi> dimidia <hi rend="spaced">abscisa sit</hi>, XL sol. <hi rend="spaced">emendentur</hi> ei.
passages.en: If <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> half <hi rend="spaced">is cut off</hi>, XL shillings <hi rend="spaced">shall be paid in compensation</hi> to him.

passages.text: Si quis costam <hi rend="spaced">hominis</hi> fregerit cute integra, emendet ei decem sol.
passages.en: If anyone breaks a rib <hi rend="spaced">of a man</hi> with the skin intact, he shall compensate him ten shillings.

passages.text: Quodsi cutis fracta fuerit, et os inde <hi rend="spaced">extrahatur</hi>, quindecim sol.
passages.en: But if the skin is broken, and bone <hi rend="spaced">is extracted</hi> from it, fifteen shillings.

passages.text: Si cui <hi rend="spaced">abscidatur</hi> oculus, pes aut manus, <hi rend="spaced">ista tria</hi> ęquale pretium <hi rend="spaced">habent, scilicet</hi> sexaginta VI solid. et sex den. et tertiam partem denarii.
passages.en: If someone's eye, foot or hand <hi rend="spaced">is cut off</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">these three</hi> <hi rend="spaced">have</hi> an equal price, <hi rend="spaced">namely</hi> sixty-six shillings and six pence and a third part of a penny.

passages.text: Si alicui abscidatur crus <hi rend="spaced">usque ad</hi> genu, octoginta sol. ei <hi rend="spaced">emendentur</hi>.
passages.en: If someone's leg is cut off <hi rend="spaced">up to</hi> the knee, eighty shillings <hi rend="spaced">shall be paid in compensation</hi> to him.

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">absciderit</hi> scapulas <hi rend="spaced">alterius</hi>, uiginti sol. emendet.
passages.en: If anyone <hi rend="spaced">cuts off</hi> the shoulders <hi rend="spaced">of another</hi>, he shall compensate twenty shillings.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">autem ita percussus fuerit</hi>, ut os inde abstrahatur, XV sol. ei emend'.
passages.en: If <hi rend="spaced">however he has been so struck</hi> that bone is drawn out from it, he shall compensate him XV shillings.

passages.text: Si grossus neruus <hi rend="spaced">incisus</hi> fuerit <hi rend="spaced">et mederi</hi> <hi rend="spaced">potest</hi>, duodecim solidi <hi rend="spaced">emendentur</hi>.
passages.en: If the great sinew <hi rend="spaced">is cut</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and it can</hi> <hi rend="spaced">be healed</hi>, twelve shillings <hi rend="spaced">shall be paid in compensation</hi>.

passages.text: Si autem claudus fuerit <hi rend="spaced">propter incisionem nerui</hi>, ita ut sanari non possit, triginta sol. emend'.
passages.en: But if he is lame <hi rend="spaced">because of the cutting of the sinew</hi>, so that he cannot be cured, he shall compensate thirty shillings.

passages.text: Si delicatiores <seg type="recension">(id est minores)</seg> nerui <hi rend="spaced">incisi fuerint</hi>, VI sol. emend'.
passages.en: If the more delicate <seg type="recension">(that is, smaller)</seg> sinews <hi rend="spaced">are cut</hi>, he shall compensate VI shillings.

passages.text: Si cui <hi rend="spaced">nerui et uenę</hi> super collum ita <hi rend="spaced">incidantur, ut non possit collum erigere, et tamen sic deformatus uiuat</hi>, centum solidi ei dentur pro emendatione, nisi sapientes maiorem illi <hi rend="spaced">rectitudinem iudicent</hi>. . . .
passages.en: If someone's <hi rend="spaced">sinews and veins</hi> on the neck are so <hi rend="spaced">cut that he cannot raise his neck, and yet he lives thus disfigured</hi>, a hundred shillings shall be given him as compensation, unless the wise <hi rend="spaced">adjudge</hi> him a greater <hi rend="spaced">right</hi>. . . .

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Si quis alii</hi><hi rend="small"> arma sua pręstiterit, et ille, <hi rend="spaced">cui pręstita sunt</hi>, inde hominem occiderit, ipse</hi><hi rend="small"> qui arma pręstitit</hi><hi rend="small"> tertiam partem pretii et forisfacturę persoluat; aut se</hi><hi rend="small"> purget, quod non fuit <hi rend="spaced">consilium nec uoluntas eius</hi>.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">If anyone has lent his weapons to another, and he <hi rend="spaced">to whom they were lent</hi> kills a man with them, he himself who lent the weapons shall pay a third part of the price and of the forfeiture; or he shall clear himself, that it was not <hi rend="spaced">his counsel nor his will</hi>.</hi>

passages.text: . . . Si canis hominem dilacerauerit aut occiderit, prima uice ille <hi rend="spaced">cuius canis est</hi> ei emendet sex sol.; et si <hi rend="spaced">post hoc</hi> eundem canem pauerit, duodecim solidos persoluat; tertia <hi rend="spaced">uero uice, si idem</hi> <hi rend="spaced">fecerit, dominus eius</hi> triginta sol. <hi rend="spaced">emendet</hi>.
passages.en: . . . If a dog tears or kills a man, the first time he <hi rend="spaced">whose dog it is</hi> shall compensate him six shillings; and if <hi rend="spaced">after this</hi> he feeds the same dog, he shall pay twelve shillings; the third <hi rend="spaced">time, however, if it</hi> <hi rend="spaced">does the same, its master</hi> shall <hi rend="spaced">compensate</hi> thirty shillings.

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">quamuis</hi> canis in tali facto perierit, tamen emendatio <hi rend="spaced">persoluatur</hi>.
passages.en: And <hi rend="spaced">although</hi> the dog perishes in such a deed, nevertheless the compensation <hi rend="spaced">shall be paid</hi>.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Quodsi canis adhuc plura</hi> <hi rend="spaced">his mala peregerit</hi>, et <hi rend="spaced">supradictus dominus</hi> <seg type="recension">(eius)</seg> illum adhuc retinuerit, emendet plenum <hi rend="spaced">pretium eius cui malum</hi> fecerit, <hi rend="spaced">siue sit uiolatio</hi> cicatricis <hi rend="spaced">siue sit</hi> <hi rend="spaced">aliud</hi> . . . .
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">But if the dog has done still more</hi> <hi rend="spaced">harms than these</hi>, and <hi rend="spaced">the aforesaid master</hi> <seg type="recension">(its)</seg> still keeps it, he shall compensate the full <hi rend="spaced">price of the one to whom harm</hi> it has done, <hi rend="spaced">whether it be the violation of</hi> a scar <hi rend="spaced">or whether it be</hi> <hi rend="spaced">something else</hi> . . . .

passages.text: Prętium <hi rend="spaced">hominis</hi>, <hi rend="bold">quem superius</hi><hi rend="bold"> nominauimus</hi> <hi rend="bold">ceorlman</hi>, secundum legem Merciorum sunt CC solidi.
passages.en: The price <hi rend="spaced">of a man</hi> <hi rend="bold">whom we have named above</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">ceorlman</hi></hi>, according to the law of the Mercians, is CC shillings.

passages.text: [43] Liberalis hominis, <hi rend="spaced">id</hi><hi rend="spaced"> est</hi> þegenes, pretium est <hi rend="spaced">sexies</hi> tantum, id est duodecies C sol.
passages.en: [43] The price of a free man of rank (thegn), <hi rend="spaced">that is</hi> of a <hi rend="italic">þegenes</hi> [thegn's], is <hi rend="spaced">six times</hi> as much, that is twelve times C shillings.

passages.text: [43, 1] Sexies autem tantum erit simplum prętium regis, hoc est <hi rend="bold">ducente</hi> XX librę.
passages.en: [43, 1] But six times as much will be the single price of the king, that is <hi rend="bold">two hundred</hi> XX pounds.

passages.text: [43, 2] Tantum secundum iustitiam est prętium <hi rend="spaced">regis</hi>.
passages.en: [43, 2] So much according to justice is the price <hi rend="spaced">of the king</hi>.

passages.text: [43, 3] Sed propter <hi rend="spaced">excellentiam</hi> regię dignitatis conuenit iterum tantundem <hi rend="spaced">dare</hi>.
passages.en: [43, 3] But because of the <hi rend="spaced">excellence</hi> of the royal dignity it is fitting <hi rend="spaced">to give</hi> again just as much.

passages.text: [43, 4] Parentes <seg type="recension">(uero)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">regis</hi> iuste <hi rend="spaced">debent habere simplum</hi> prętium eius <seg type="recension">(regis)</seg> et populus <hi rend="spaced">aliud</hi>.
passages.en: [43, 4] The kinsmen <seg type="recension">(however)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">of the king</hi> justly <hi rend="spaced">ought to have the single</hi> price of him <seg type="recension">(the king)</seg>, and the people the <hi rend="spaced">other</hi>.

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Sacramentum liberalis</hi><hi rend="small"> hominis, <hi rend="spaced">quem</hi></hi><hi rend="small"><hi rend="spaced"> quidem</hi></hi><hi rend="small"><hi rend="spaced"> Angli</hi></hi><hi rend="small"><hi rend="spaced"> uocant</hi></hi><hi rend="small"> tƿelfhende</hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(man</hi><hi rend="small">)</hi></seg><hi rend="small">, <hi rend="spaced">debet stare et</hi> ualere iuramentum sex</hi><hi rend="small"> uillanorum, quia</hi><hi rend="small"> prętium eius est</hi><hi rend="small">, id est ƿeregeld</hi><hi rend="small">, sex</hi><hi rend="small"> uillanorum.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">The oath of a noble, <hi rend="spaced">whom</hi><hi rend="spaced"> indeed</hi><hi rend="spaced"> the English</hi><hi rend="spaced"> call</hi> <hi rend="italic">tƿelfhende</hi></hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(man)</hi></seg><hi rend="small">, <hi rend="spaced">ought to stand and</hi> be worth the oath of six villeins, because his price, that is <hi rend="italic">ƿeregeld</hi> [wergeld], is [that] of six villeins.</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Sacramentum presbiteri</hi> regulariter <hi rend="small">uiuentis tantundem ualet </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(scilicet</hi><hi rend="small">)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> sicut liberalis hominis, propter septem ęcclesiasticos ordines.</hi>
