passages.en: <hi rend="small">The oath of a priest</hi> regularly [by a rule] <hi rend="small">living is worth just as much </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(namely)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> as [that] of a noble, on account of the seven ecclesiastical orders.</hi>

passages.text: Septem <hi rend="spaced">enim</hi> dona sunt Spiritus sancti; et septies <hi rend="spaced">presbiteri et alii serui Dei in</hi> <hi rend="spaced">ęcclesiis</hi> debent cotidie Deum laudare et pro populo Christiano iugiter interuenire.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">For</hi> there are seven gifts of the Holy Spirit; and seven times daily <hi rend="spaced">priests and other servants of God in</hi> <hi rend="spaced">churches</hi> ought to praise God and continually intercede for the Christian people.

passages.text: Et propterea quisquis talibus nocere <hi rend="spaced">cupit aut fecit, oportet</hi> eum septupla emendatione illud emendare.
passages.en: And therefore whoever <hi rend="spaced">desires or has done</hi> harm to such, <hi rend="spaced">it is necessary</hi> that he make amends for it with sevenfold compensation.

passages.text: [45, 2] [2—8] Et si <hi rend="spaced">aliquis presbiterum occiderit, excepto eius</hi> iusto prętio, <hi rend="spaced">pro unoquoque ordine</hi> uiginti sol. emendet, uide<hi rend="spaced">licet ad ordinem ostiarii</hi> uiginti sol., item <hi rend="spaced">ad exorcistam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">iterum</hi> uiginti sol., et sic <hi rend="spaced">per ordinem</hi>, usque <hi rend="spaced">transeat presbiteratum</hi>. [45, 3] <hi rend="spaced">Istę septem librę pro septem ordinibus erunt extra prętium quod dicitur</hi> þeregeld.
passages.en: [45, 2] [2—8] And if <hi rend="spaced">anyone kills a priest, besides his</hi> just price, he shall compensate <hi rend="spaced">for each order</hi> twenty shillings, <hi rend="spaced">namely for the order of doorkeeper</hi> twenty shillings, likewise <hi rend="spaced">for the exorcist</hi> <hi rend="spaced">again</hi> twenty shillings, and so <hi rend="spaced">through the orders</hi>, until <hi rend="spaced">it passes the priesthood</hi>. [45, 3] <hi rend="spaced">These seven pounds for the seven orders will be outside the price which is called</hi> <hi rend="italic">þeregeld</hi>.

passages.text: [9, 1] Et erunt <seg type="recension">(iste)</seg> iuste episcopi <hi rend="bold">et pauperum.</hi>
passages.en: [9, 1] And <seg type="recension">(these)</seg> shall justly be the bishop's <hi rend="bold">and the poor's.</hi>

passages.text: Istę sunt consuetudines regum inter Anglos:
passages.en: These are the customs of the kings among the English:

passages.text: Omnes rectitudines ciuitatum <seg type="recension">(regis sunt)</seg>; et pastum [suum cum omnibus rebus quę ad illum pastum pertinent; carta alodii ad ęternam hęreditatem; forisfactura alodii; et prętium eorum qui habent alodium, quando ita profunde forisfaciunt se ipsos; forisfactura belli, quod Angli uocant ferdƿíte in terra omnium suorum;
passages.en: All the rights of the cities <seg type="recension">(are the king's)</seg>; and his food-rent [with all the things that pertain to that food-rent; the charter of allod (bookland) for eternal inheritance; the forfeiture of allod; and the price of those who hold allod, when they forfeit themselves so deeply; the forfeiture for war, which the English call <hi rend="italic">ferdƿíte</hi> [fyrd-wite], in the land of all his men;

passages.text: pastio proclamati exulis, quod Angli dicunt <seg type="recension">(uocant)</seg> bebodenes utlage;
passages.en: the feeding of a proclaimed exile, which the English say <seg type="recension">(call)</seg> <hi rend="italic">bebodenes utlage</hi> [a commanded outlaw];

passages.text: pastio etiam latronum latitantium in siluis qui spoliant et occidunt alios <seg type="recension">(homines)</seg> — quos Angli uocant fléman —; omnis latro extra proclamatus; uita aut prętium publici latronis.
passages.en: also the feeding of robbers hiding in the woods who plunder and kill others <seg type="recension">(men)</seg> — whom the English call <hi rend="italic">fléman</hi> [fugitives] —; every robber proclaimed outside [the law]; the life or the price of a public robber.

passages.text: Inuasio domus uel curię, quod dicitur rihthamsócne, si ille qui fecerit proclamatus fuerit extra terminos suos, tunc si uenerit ad emendationem, rex illam habebit.
passages.en: Invasion of a house or court, which is called <hi rend="italic">rihthamsócne</hi> [true hamsocn], if he who has done it has been proclaimed outside his bounds, then, if he comes to make amends, the king shall have it.

passages.text: Fractionem etiam pacis, quod dicitur grithbrece: si pax ex parte regis pręcipitur in comitatu uel in hundredo, qui post illam fregerit, regi emendabit.
passages.en: Also breach of the peace, which is called <hi rend="italic">grithbrece</hi> [grith-breach]: if peace is commanded on the king's part in the shire (court) or in the hundred, whoever breaks it after that shall make amends to the king.

passages.text: Emendatio fracti pontis in uia regia.
passages.en: The amends for a broken bridge on the king's road.

passages.text: In terra omnium secundum antiquam consuetudinem fractę pacis ęcclesię emendatio erit communiter regis et episcopi.
passages.en: In the land of all men, according to ancient custom, the amends for broken peace of the church shall be in common the king's and the bishop's.

passages.text: Et multas alias consuetudines habet rex, quę sibi conueniunt.
passages.en: And the king has many other customs which befit him.

passages.text: Qui diuisionem habet iuxta terram regis, claudat contra regem aut custodiat aut dilectione aut prętio adquirat, si uoluerit aliquam <seg type="recension">(commoditatem)</seg> in terra illa aisiam habere.
passages.en: Whoever has a boundary next to the king's land, let him fence against the king or keep watch, or acquire it by goodwill or by price, if he wishes to have any <seg type="recension">(advantage)</seg> easement in that land.

passages.text: Antiqua consuetudo fuit, ut omnis ęcclesiastica et secularis emendatio communis erat regi et episcopo.
passages.en: It was an ancient custom that every ecclesiastical and secular amends was common to the king and the bishop.

passages.text: Hoc etiam debet quisque scire, quia, si pro aliqua forisfactura, quę ad Deum pertineat, accipitur pecunia ab episcopo uel ab aliquo alio, episcopus debet eandem pecuniam distribuere ęcclesiis et pauperibus.
passages.en: This too each man ought to know, that, if for any forfeiture which pertains to God money is taken by the bishop or by any other, the bishop ought to distribute that same money to churches and to the poor.

passages.text: Comitis rectitudines secundum Anglos istę sunt communes cum rege: tertius denarius in uillis ubi mercatum conuenerit et in castigatione latronum; et comitales uillas quę pertinent ad comitatum eius; et consuetudines liberalium hominum duppliciter omnes habere, uidelicet duplicem mundam, duplicem manbote et forisfacturam <seg type="recension">(duplicem)</seg>; duplex etiam habere debet prętium, id est þere.
passages.en: The earl's rights according to the English, these are common with the king: the third penny in towns where a market has come together and in the punishment of thieves; and the comital towns which pertain to his shire; and to have all the customs of free men of rank (thegns) doubly, namely double <hi rend="italic">mund</hi> [protection], double <hi rend="italic">manbote</hi> [man-amends] and <seg type="recension">(double)</seg> forfeiture; he must also have a double price, that is <hi rend="italic">þere</hi> [wer].

passages.text: <hi rend="small">In lege Cantia</hi><hi rend="small"> Ęcclesia Christi et rex et archiepiscopus habent similem et ęque carum despectum, </hi><hi rend="spaced"><hi rend="small">quod Angli dicunt</hi></hi><hi rend="small"> mundbrece</hi><hi rend="small">.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">In the law of Kent Christ Church and the king and the archbishop have a like and equally dear contempt-fine, </hi><hi rend="spaced"><hi rend="small">which the English call</hi></hi><hi rend="small"> <hi rend="italic">mundbrece</hi> [breach of protection].</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Et in illa lege pecunia archiepiscopi undecies <hi rend="spaced">reddetur</hi>, pecunia autem</hi><hi rend="small"> regis <hi rend="spaced">non</hi> reddetur <hi rend="spaced">nisi</hi> nouies.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">And in that law the archbishop's property <hi rend="spaced">shall be repaid</hi> elevenfold, but the king's property shall <hi rend="spaced">not</hi> be repaid <hi rend="spaced">except</hi> ninefold.</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Ali[a]s</hi><hi rend="small"> archiepiscopus et <hi rend="spaced">filius regis</hi></hi><hi rend="small"> <hi rend="spaced">de legali coniuge habent similem secularem rectitudinem</hi></hi> in multis rebus, <hi rend="small">hoc est in despectu</hi><hi rend="small">,</hi> in emendatione hominis occisi, quod dicitur manbote, et in multis aliis diuersis rebus, id est þere prętio reddendo et forisfactura<seg type="recension">(m)</seg>, utroque ęque magnum et carum.
passages.en: <hi rend="small">Other[wise] the archbishop and the <hi rend="spaced">king's son</hi> <hi rend="spaced">by a lawful wife have a like secular right</hi></hi> in many things, <hi rend="small">that is in the contempt-fine,</hi> in the amends for a slain man, which is called <hi rend="italic">manbote</hi> [man-amends], and in many other different things, that is in paying the <hi rend="italic">þere</hi> [wer] price and the forfeiture<seg type="recension">(m)</seg>, both equally great and dear.

passages.text: Episcopus et comes habent multas seculares leges ęquales; etiam omnia olim idem habuerunt propter excellentiam ordinis.
passages.en: The bishop and the earl have many equal secular laws; indeed formerly they had all the same, on account of the excellence of their order.

passages.text: Episcopi inprimis ęcclesiasticam <seg type="recension">(habeant)</seg> correctionem et Christianam dominationem super omnes, quos <hi rend="small">debent</hi><hi rend="small"> docere et ante iudicium Dei eos ducere et</hi> pręire.
passages.en: Bishops above all <seg type="recension">(should have)</seg> ecclesiastical correction and Christian lordship over all, whom they <hi rend="small">ought to teach and to lead before the judgment of God and</hi> to go before.

passages.text: In multis tamen locis secundum iusticiam in sua propria terra et in suis uillis debent habere constitutionem hundredi, quod Angli dicunt hundrædsétene; et prętium latronum infra terminos eorum <seg type="recension">(proclamatorum)</seg>; et infectam inuasionem, quod Angli dicunt <seg type="recension">(dicitur)</seg> unƿorhtre hamsocne; et toll ⁊ team; et correctionem latronum, quousque sit condemnatus ad mortem;
passages.en: In many places, however, according to justice, in their own land and in their towns they ought to have the setting of the hundred, which the English call <hi rend="italic">hundrædsétene</hi> [hundred-session]; and the price of thieves <seg type="recension">(proclaimed)</seg> within their bounds; and unaccomplished invasion, which the English call <seg type="recension">(which is called)</seg> <hi rend="italic">unƿorhtre hamsocne</hi> [attempted hamsocn]; and <hi rend="italic">toll ⁊ team</hi>; and the correction of thieves, until he is condemned to death;

passages.text: sic etiam monetarios et púndæres uel ponderatores; et loca iudiciorum ferri aut aquę; proprias mensuras et pondera; et multas uarias consuetudines, quas statuerunt qúi Dei honorem <seg type="recension">(et iustitiam)</seg> amauerunt.
passages.en: so also moneyers and <hi rend="italic">púndæres</hi> or weighers; and places of the ordeals of iron or water; their own measures and weights; and many various customs, which those established who loved God's honour <seg type="recension">(and justice)</seg>.

passages.text: [60] <hi rend="spaced">Antiqua</hi> <hi rend="bold">lex Anglorum</hi> fuit, quod <hi rend="spaced">gens</hi> <hi rend="spaced">illorúm</hi> et consuetudines in honore tenebantur; et <hi rend="bold">per consilium</hi> dabantur <seg type="recension">(uni-)</seg> cuique secundum mensuram cuiusque <hi rend="spaced">comiti et uillano</hi>, liberali et <hi rend="bold">subliberali.</hi>
passages.en: [60] It was an <hi rend="spaced">ancient</hi> <hi rend="bold">law of the English</hi> that <hi rend="spaced">their</hi> <hi rend="spaced">people</hi> and customs were held in honour; and <hi rend="bold">by counsel</hi> [rights] were given to <seg type="recension">(every)</seg> each according to the measure of each, <hi rend="spaced">to earl and villein</hi>, to the free man of rank (thegn) and to the <hi rend="bold">lesser free man</hi>.

passages.text: [60, 1] Et si uillanus ita creuisset <hi rend="bold">sua probitate,</hi> quod pleniter haberet quinque hídas de suo próprio <hi rend="spaced">alodio</hi> <hi rend="bold">et ęcclesiam propriam</hi> et clocarium <hi rend="bold">et coquinam</hi> et portam, sedem et priuatum profectum in aula regis, tunc deinde erat dignus honore liberalitatis, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> þegen<hi rend="bold">scipes</hi> þurðe.
passages.en: [60, 1] And if a villein had so prospered <hi rend="bold">by his own worth</hi> that he fully had five hides of his own <hi rend="spaced">allod</hi> <hi rend="bold">and his own church</hi> and bell-house <hi rend="bold">and kitchen</hi> and gate, a seat and special office in the king's hall, then thenceforth he was worthy of the honour of nobility, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þegen<hi rend="bold">scipes</hi> þurðe</hi> [worthy of thegnship].

passages.text: [61] <hi rend="bold">Si</hi> autem liberalis homo, id est þegen, <hi rend="spaced">ita profecisset</hi>, ut regi seruisset et <hi rend="spaced">uice sua</hi> equitaret in <hi rend="bold">missiático</hi> regis, is talis, si haberet <hi rend="spaced">alium sub sé</hi>, qui ad <hi rend="bold">expeditionem</hi> regis quinque hidas teneret et in aula regis suo domino seruisset et ter nuntius domini sui regem adisset, is, <hi rend="spaced">inquam</hi>, talis dehinc <hi rend="spaced">potest</hi> pro domino suo preiurare iuramentum, <hi rend="bold">quod supra</hi><hi rend="bold"> nominauimus</hi> foraþ, <hi rend="bold">in diuersis rebus,</hi> ubicunque opus est.
passages.en: [61] <hi rend="bold">If</hi> moreover a free man of rank, that is a <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi> [thegn], <hi rend="spaced">had so advanced</hi> that he served the king and rode <hi rend="spaced">in his stead</hi> on the king's <hi rend="bold">mission</hi>, such a one, if he had <hi rend="spaced">another under him</hi> who held five hides for the king's <hi rend="bold">expedition</hi> and had served his lord in the king's hall and had three times gone to the king as his lord's messenger, such a one, <hi rend="spaced">I say</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">can</hi> thenceforth swear the fore-oath for his lord, <hi rend="bold">which we named above</hi> <hi rend="italic">foraþ</hi> [fore-oath], <hi rend="bold">in various matters,</hi> wherever there is need.

passages.text: [61, 1] Qui autem talem non haberet, per semetipsum id <hi rend="spaced">faceret aut</hi> caréret.
passages.en: [61, 1] But whoever did not have such a one would <hi rend="spaced">do</hi> it by himself <hi rend="spaced">or</hi> go without.

passages.text: [61, 2] Et si liberalis homo ita ascendisset, ut comes fieret, habebat <hi rend="spaced">omnes rectitudines suas sicut</hi> comes.
passages.en: [61, 2] And if a free man of rank had so risen that he became an earl, he had <hi rend="spaced">all his rights as</hi> an earl.

passages.text: [62] Si mercator ter mare transisset suo proprio sumptu, talis deinde erat liberalitate dignus, <hi rend="spaced">quod dicunt</hi> þegenrihtes þurðe.
passages.en: [62] If a merchant had three times crossed the sea at his own expense, such a one was thenceforth worthy of nobility, <hi rend="spaced">which they call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þegenrihtes þurðe</hi> [worthy of thegn-right].

passages.text: [63] Ita <hi rend="spaced">etiam</hi> et clericus, qui discendo tantum profecerat, ut ordines haberet et <hi rend="bold">in castitate</hi> Christo seruiret, is tunc iudicabatur <hi rend="spaced">iure in omnibus</hi> <hi rend="bold">liberalitatem</hi> habere debere.
passages.en: [63] So <hi rend="spaced">also</hi> a cleric too, who by learning had advanced so far that he had orders and served Christ <hi rend="bold">in chastity</hi>, he was then judged <hi rend="spaced">by right in all things</hi> to be bound to have <hi rend="bold">nobility</hi>.

passages.text: [63, 1] Et si <hi rend="bold">contigerit</hi>, aliquem nocuisse ordinato aut peregrino, tunc rex et episcopus <hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi>, quam citius possent, hoc deberent emendare.
passages.en: [63, 1] And if it <hi rend="bold">should happen</hi> that someone has injured an ordained man or a stranger, then the king and the bishop ought <hi rend="spaced">justly</hi> to make amends for it as quickly as they could.

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Cornu bouis <hi rend="spaced">persoluitur</hi> decem denariis et uaccę duobus denariis;</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">The horn of an ox <hi rend="spaced">is paid for</hi> with ten pence and of a cow with two pence;</hi>

passages.en: <hi rend="small">the tail </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(however)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> of an ox </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(is paid for)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> with one shilling and of a cow </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(is paid for)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> with five pence; the eye of an ox </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(is paid for)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> with five pence and of a cow</hi> four <seg type="recension">(pence)</seg>.
